docs.title: Paladio documentation
docs.text:
Paladio is a self-hosted travel planning, route optimization, and fare telemetry platform built with FastAPI, Next.js 16, PostgreSQL 16 (with TimescaleDB and pgvector), Redis, Celery, Valhalla, and a C++20 combinatorial core (paladio_core). Trip generation, booking parsing, and 768-dimensional semantic search run deterministically on local infrastructure without external generative Large Language Model (LLM) APIs, while an optional interactive assistant supports 13 LLM providers and an 82-tool Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

  • Getting started

    Deploy the 7-container Docker stack, run first-time provisioning at /setup, calibrate your 8-axis Taste Star, and compile paladio_core locally.

    Start with installation

  • User guide

    Explore Control Center, New Trip creation, the Trip Workspace map and Speed Dial, public transit GTFS, the Bookings Wallet, Route Monitoring (experimental), Costs, Trip Archive, and the optional AI assistant.

    Explore the user guide

  • Self-hosting and operations

    Configure .env bootstrap keys and /config dynamic settings, manage city POI and GTFS storage, set up reverse proxies, integrate Immich or Synology, and maintain backups.

    Read operator runbooks

  • System architecture

    Inspect the 8-stage deterministic Itinerary v2 pipeline, 9-node LangGraph swarm, C++20 TCOPTW branch-and-bound solver, CPU ONNX retrieval, and Deal Engine architecture.

    Study the architecture

  • Technical reference

    Look up exact REST endpoints, WebSocket message schemas, all 82 MCP tools, 54 database tables, 18 Celery tasks, C++20/Python signatures, and the .trip archive schema.

    Browse technical reference

  • Contributing

    Follow Paladio's dynamic-data and zero-legacy engineering rules, 10-locale translation parity checks, pre-commit hooks, and GitHub Wiki sync workflow.

    Read the developer guide

docs.title: Documentation portals
docs.text:
Paladio ships three synchronized documentation surfaces so end users, homelab operators, and contributors can each reach verified answers without leaving their environment:

  • Documentation site: Built with Material for MkDocs from docs/ and published to leandro-juan.github.io/paladio.
  • GitHub Wiki: Generated directly from mkdocs.yml via scripts/sync_wiki.py at github.com/Leandro-Juan/paladio/wiki.
  • In-app Help Center: Embedded inside the web UI at /help with 10 categories, 22 articles, screenshots, and interactive mockups translated across all 10 shipped locales.

docs.title: Interactive AI agent and MCP safety model
docs.text: Paladio exposes 82 trip-manipulation tools over FastMCP (/mcp HTTP and stdio) and drives the interactive Plan -> Agent chat assistant (TripAgentRunner) with tiered write confirmations, turn locking, DNS-rebinding checks, and full audit logging.

docs.title: Tool execution pipeline and InstrumentedMCPToolset
docs.text:
Inside backend/app/agent/runner.py, pydantic_ai.Agent connects directly to the in-process FastMCP server through InstrumentedMCPToolset under a scoped user context (with_user_context). Every tool call emits structured WebSocket events (tool_call, tool_result, proposal, trip_updated) over /api/ws/trip-agent/{trip_id} so the UI shows live progress without polling.

  • Dynamic toolset gating (backend/app/agent/toolsets.py): Turns start with 21 core tools (CORE_TOOLS) to keep context windows small and fast across local and cloud LLMs, dynamically activating up to 9 specialized domain toolsets (expenses, tickets, transit, collab, collections, market, jobs, engine, itinerary_advanced) from message keywords or load_toolset.
  • 90s exclusive turn lock & live cancellation: Redis key paladio:agent:lock:{trip_id} prevents concurrent chat turns on the same trip, while register_cancel_token wires an asyncio.Event so users can abort mid-stream.

docs.title: Three-tier safety classification (Read / Tier W / Tier C)
docs.text:
Tools are annotated with explicit MCP metadata (readOnlyHint, idempotentHint, destructiveHint) and enforced server-side before modifying PostgreSQL.

Safety tier Behavior Representative tools Read & Simulate (Read) Executes immediately; never mutates DB; wallet secrets masked get_trip_overview, get_itinerary, search_pois, what_if, compare_metrics, list_tickets Routine Write (Tier W) Executes immediately under EDITOR/OWNER RBAC; snapshots trip_revisions + broadcasts paladio:trip:{trip_id} + returns undo token add_stop, move_stop, lock_stop, set_stop_time, optimize_day, add_expense, create_ticket Confirmation Gate (Tier C) Unless invoked with confirmed=true after approval, stores a Redis proposal (paladio:proposal:{id}, 600s TTL) with diff summary and pauses for user approve / reject remove_stop (locked or flight/hotel anchors), swap_days, remove_day, optimize_trip, rebalance_days, fit_to_budget, delete_ticket, delete_expense, remove_participant, change_hotel_anchor, update_trip_details (destination/dates), export_trip_package (community_shareable)

docs.title: Revision snapshots, audit trail, and HTTP hardening
docs.text:
Every mutation executed through the agent or MCP server stays reversible and cryptographically auditable:

  • Immutable trip_revisions & Undo: Mutating tools record full before/after itinerary snapshots in trip_revisions, enabling instant 1-step (undo_last_change) or target-revision (undo_to) rollbacks.
  • Audit trail (agent_actions): backend/app/mcp/audit.py logs tool invocations with user ID, trip ID, outcome, and SHA-256-hashed arguments without leaking sensitive raw payloads.
  • Network & auth isolation: verify_origin_and_host (backend/app/mcp/auth.py) enforces Host and Origin allowlists (localhost, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0) on Streamable HTTP /mcp requests alongside Bearer JWT verification (PALADIO_API_TOKEN for stdio).

docs.title: C++20 combinatorial core (paladio_core)
docs.text: cpp_core/ implements three deterministic, GIL-releasing routing solvers in zero-dependency C++20 exposed to Python through pybind11: an exact Time-Constrained Orienteering Problem with Time Windows (TCOPTW) branch-and-bound optimizer (optimize_itinerary), a full-visit TSP tour heuristic (solve_tsp_tour), and a soft-time-window TSPTW re-optimizer (solve_tsptw).

docs.title: Why combinatorial optimization lives in C++20
docs.text:
Solving daily itineraries inside Python loops hits Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) contention and dynamic allocation overhead during deep search trees. Moving route optimization into paladio::core gives Paladio deterministic millisecond latency across concurrent trip requests while freeing Python threads via py::gil_scoped_release.

Algorithmic scope of cpp_core/

All three solvers consume precomputed row-major flattened N x N transit duration (int32) and cost (float64) arrays supplied by Valhalla, GTFS, or Haversine matrices in Python. cpp_core/ does not implement interval trees, spatial Haversine indices, Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS), or Simulated Annealing.

docs.title: Exact TCOPTW solver (optimize_itinerary, \(N \le 64\))
docs.text:
optimize_itinerary performs an exact Depth-First Branch & Bound search maximizing net utility score subject to monetary budget, hard opening/closing time windows, global end deadlines, mandatory stop inclusion, and human physiological rules.

flowchart TD
    Pre["Pre-sort POIs by score/duration density\nBuild uint64_t mandatory mask & min_transit_global"] --> DFS["Stack-allocated SearchState (~336 bytes)"]
    DFS --> Guard["Timeout & max_nodes_expanded check (every 1,024 nodes)"]
    Guard --> Bound["Continuous Fractional Knapsack Upper Bound\nvia std::countr_zero(unvisited)"]
    Bound -->|"current + bound < best - 1e-5"| Prune["Prune branch"]
    Bound -->|"Promising"| Pareto["Multi-Criteria Pareto Dominance Check\non (visited_mask, node)"]
    Pareto -->|"Dominated"| Prune
    Pareto -->|"Dominant"| Mand["Mandatory POI Reachability & End-Depot Lookahead"]
    Mand -->|"Feasible"| Recurse["Apply physiological penalties & recurse in-place"]
  • Zero-copy DFS frame: SearchState packs uint64_t visited_mask, std::array<int, 64> path and arrival buffers, category/taxonomy counters, fatigue minutes, and meal timestamps into roughly 336 bytes on the stack, mutating and restoring fields in place without path heap allocations. (Pareto dominance memoization maps (visited_mask, node) buckets in std::unordered_map<MemoKey, std::vector<MemoEntry>>.)
  • Continuous fractional knapsack bound: Unvisited nodes are traversed in descending score / duration density order using C++20 <bit> std::countr_zero, lower-bounding transit with min_transit_global and permitting one fractional final POI inside remaining time.
  • Multi-criteria Pareto dominance: Prunes partial tours at (visited_mask, u) whenever an existing memoized state reaches u with <= time, <= cost, >= score - 1e-5, a superset of meal flags, <= continuous_active_time, and matching last_meal_time.
  • Physiological human-realism constraints: Enforces breakfast_deadline, lunch_deadline, dinner_deadline, min_meal_spacing, max_idle_time, idle penalty (idle_time / 15.0 * idle_time_penalty_rate), max_active_time_before_fatigue reset on HOTEL/BAR/meals, and exponential category monotony damping across 16 category_id slots.
  • Lexicographical tie-breaking: Maximizes total_score (epsilon 1e-5), then minimizes total_time, then minimizes total_cost.

docs.title: Full-visit TSP and soft-window TSPTW re-optimizers
docs.text:
When you drag stops, lock anchors, and click Solve inside the workspace (TripReoptimizationService), every stop in that day must remain in the tour (N is unconstrained by the 64-bit mask limit):

  1. solve_tsp_tour: Pins start_node (and optionally end_node when fixed_end=True), builds up to 4 multi-start Nearest-Neighbor tours from nearest first-hop neighbors, and refines them with asymmetric-safe 2-opt (up to 100 passes) and Or-opt block relocations (L = 1, 2, 3, up to 20 passes each).
  2. solve_tsptw: Initializes tours from Earliest Deadline First (EDF) plus up to 4 time-window Nearest-Neighbor starts, then runs up to 100 joint 2-opt and Or-opt (L = 1, 2) passes minimizing total directed transit plus quadratic lateness penalties (penalty_weight * (reach - window_end)^2) and linear earliness wait penalties (0.5 * (window_start - reach)).

docs.title: Measured performance characteristics
docs.text:
Benchmarks documented in cpp_core/docs/benchmarks.md (Ryzen 7 7730U, GCC 13.3.0 -O3 -DNDEBUG -march=native -fno-rtti) show sub-millisecond solving on small daily graphs and predictable scaling under constrained time windows; in backend production calls, max_nodes_expanded (default 50,000 in Itinerary v2) and timeout_ms guard worst-case dense graphs by returning the best incumbent with timed_out = true.

Graph size (\(N\)) Window / density profile Documented mean latency \(N = 10\) Daily subgraph 5.5 us \(N = 25\) Typical city day 1.31 ms mean (2.05 ms P95) \(N = 64\) 4-hour window 2.54 ms \(N = 64\) Dense full-day graph (unbounded) 2.74 s

See C++20 and Python API reference for exact signatures and parameter defaults.

docs.title: Deal Engine and multi-modal transit architecture
docs.text: Two self-hosted subsystems keep Paladio independent of commercial itinerary aggregators: a TimescaleDB-backed flight and lodging Deal Engine that scores packages against P10 quantile baselines and realism gates, and a 14-table local GTFS + Valhalla + 5-tier fare transit stack.

docs.title: Continuous flight and lodging Deal Engine
docs.text:
backend/app/engine/market/ runs scheduled daily sweeps (03:00 UTC) and on-demand route backfills to catch statistically rare price drops rather than noisy promotional banners.

Experimental data scraping

While the quantile baseline, verdict, and itinerary gating pipeline is deterministic, the flight and lodging data scraping layer is currently experimental and subject to upstream provider changes.

flowchart LR
    Flights["Aviasales Cache API + Ryanair Public API"] --> Ticks["TimescaleDB market_price_ticks"]
    Ticks --> Daily["price_daily & route_baselines (q02..q90)"]
    Daily --> Verdict["Verdict & Detector (P10 / R_MAX / Min Savings)"]
    Verdict --> Verifier["Live Fare Verifier + Lodging ProviderRouter"]
    Lodging["Booking / Google Travel / Agoda / Trip.com"] --> Verifier
    Verifier --> Gate["SovereignItineraryGate (Realism >= 8.0)"]
    Gate --> Alerts["deal_candidates & Redis paladio:events & Push Relays"]
  • Time-series quantile baselines: market_price_ticks (TimescaleDB hypertable with compression) aggregates into price_daily and route_baselines across 6 booking lead-time buckets (0–7, 8–21, 22–60, 61–120, 121–240, 241+ days) with 7 quantiles (q02, q05, q10, q25, q50, q75, q90) over a 540-day window and hierarchical fallback (full, drop_lead, drop_month).
  • Lodging sharding and entity resolution: ShardPlanner, LodgingAggregator, and EntityResolver query BookingScraperProvider, GoogleTravelHotelsProvider, AgodaProvider, TripComProvider, and HistoryQuoteProvider through ProviderRouter (circuit breakers at 5 failures / 24-hour cooldown and daily tier call budgets), deduplicating cross-provider hotels and scoring candidates via taste-aware weights (price 0.30, quality 0.25, location 0.20, taste 0.15, flexibility 0.05, trust 0.05).
  • Feasibility and realism gating: Candidates passing MIN_ABS_SAVINGS_CENTS (30.00 EUR), flight dead-window checks (00:00–05:00 local), MIN_ON_GROUND_HOURS (36 hours), and LODGING_MIN_QUALITY (70.0) must clear SovereignItineraryGate (REALISM_MIN >= 8.0) before firing alerts or pairing with public holidays (DealPackageService).

docs.title: Multi-modal transit and 5-tier fare engine
docs.text:
Paladio derives local transit feeds into indexed relational tables instead of keeping heavy graph engines loaded for every city on Earth simultaneously.

  1. Valhalla street graphs: OSMMapService downloads OSM extracts into valhalladata (/custom_files), powering local walking, cycling, and driving legs plus N x N solver distance matrices.
  2. GTFS ingestion and 14-table derivation: GTFSResolverService + build_city_gtfs_task fetch and sanitize feeds into gtfsdata, then TransitDerivationService normalizes agencies, lines, stations, patterns, stops, pattern trips, station-line links, service summaries, service calendar days, shapes, transfers, and fare tables directly in PostgreSQL (transit_*).
  3. Transitous live fallback: TransitousService queries MOTIS transit routing with Redis caching whenever a destination lacks compiled local GTFS coverage (UNAVAILABLE in transit_coverage).
  4. 5-tier FareResolver: Estimates leg fares and daily pass recommendations (get_transit_pass_advice) from compiled GTFS fare rules, dedicated adapters (Tokyo ODPT and London TfL), and cited official transit_fare_quotes (reseeded by scripts/migrate_verified_fares_to_quotes.py).

docs.title: Deterministic trip engine and LangGraph swarm
docs.text: Paladio generates itineraries through a 9-node deterministic LangGraph state machine driving an 8-stage Itinerary v2 pipeline and a critic-repair refinement loop, combining LangGraph checkpointing with zero generative LLM reliance.

docs.title: The 9-node deterministic LangGraph swarm
docs.text:
Mounted at app.state.graph (backend/app/swarm/graph.py) and driven over WS /api/ws/stream, the swarm converts unstructured trip inputs and uploaded bookings into validated, realism-audited schedules.

flowchart LR
    Start(["START"]) --> TP["ticket_parser"]
    TP --> AC["assemble_constraints"]
    AC --> VC{"verify_constraints\n(HITL #1 interrupt)"}
    VC --> GR{"guardrails\n(Hard checks + HITL #2)"}
    GR -->|"ABORT / END"| End(["END"])
    GR -->|"PROCEED"| PA["prompt_analyzer"]
    PA --> PS["planner_scrape"]
    PS --> PO["planner_optimize"]
    PO --> PC{"planner_critic\n(Objective J)"}
    PC -->|"Issues & iter < 3"| PR["planner_repair"]
    PR --> PO
    PC -->|"Clean or iter = 3"| End
Swarm node Deterministic responsibility Key design note ticket_parser Extracts flight windows, IATA codes, and hotel anchors from booking text Replaced earlier Pydantic AI LLM parsing with deterministic regex/date parsers assemble_constraints Normalizes dates, airports, budget, and depot fields into TravelConstraints Validates structure via Pydantic before downstream DB or C++ execution verify_constraints Triggers LangGraph interrupt({"type": "VERIFICATION_REQUIRED", …}) Bypassed automatically when auto_verify=True guardrails Rejects past dates, return < start, identical origin/dest, or trips > 30 days; raises TRIP_OVERLAP_WARNING interrupt on DB date collision Prevents infeasible or accidentally overlapping trips before scraping prompt_analyzer Runs PromptIntentExtractor (ONNX 768-D anchor projection + rapidfuzz POI matching) and merges participant taste vectors Extracts tastes, cuisines, pace, and mandatory POIs in milliseconds with zero LLM tokens planner_scrape Executes FetchTravelContextUseCase to ensure destination city POIs, ratings, and embeddings exist Hydrates missing city data dynamically from OSM and Wikimedia planner_optimize Executes OptimizeDailyItineraryUseCase running the 8-stage Itinerary v2 pipeline Dispatches per-day subgraphs concurrently into C++20 paladio_core planner_critic Audits realism issues (MISSING_TIER_1, DAY_OVERLOADED, DAY_UNDERLOADED, MEAL_GAP, EXCESSIVE_TRANSIT, IDLE_GAP, ZIGZAG_ROUTING) and scores J Evaluates 2-opt geometry (zigzag ratio > 1.25) to catch ping-pong routes planner_repair Applies targeted deterministic fixes and re-routes to planner_optimize Bounded at MAX_REFINEMENT_ITERATIONS = 3

Checkpointer volatility across backend restarts

create_swarm() uses LangGraph's in-memory MemorySaver by default. If api restarts mid-generation while paused at a VERIFICATION_REQUIRED or TRIP_OVERLAP_WARNING interrupt, resume requires starting a fresh trip generation request from /engine.

docs.title: Objective score \(J\) in planner_critic
docs.text:
evaluate_itinerary_quality in backend/app/swarm/critic.py quantifies itinerary realism deterministically after each optimization pass:

\[ J = (\text{total\_sights} \times 100.0) - (\text{total\_travel\_mins} \times 1.5) - \left(\sum_{i \in \text{issues}} i.\text{severity} \times 50.0\right) \times \frac{\text{critic\_strictness}}{0.75} \]

docs.title: The 8-stage Itinerary v2 pipeline
docs.text:
Inside backend/app/engine/pipeline.py, run_itinerary_v2_pipeline breaks multi-day trip planning into eight composable stages so C++ branch-and-bound sees compact, well-clustered daily subgraphs (N <= 64) rather than an intractable city-wide graph:

  1. Trip frame (build_trip_frame): Computes usable daily time windows from flight arrival/departure hours, hotel depot coordinates (defaulting to the coordinate-wise median of Tier 1/2 sights if unanchored), pace caps, and local dining rhythms (compute_city_rhythm_profile).
  2. Candidate pool (build_candidate_pool): Gathers 100% of Tier 1/2 sights, top personalized POIs scored by 768-D taste similarity + hybrid quality, mandatory stops, and candidate meal venues.
  3. Trip-level submodular selection (select_trip_pois): Locks mandatory and iconic stops first, then runs submodular greedy selection balancing category diversity against utility.
  4. Day assignment (assign_pois_to_days): Groups sights into walking bundles and anchor seeds using regret-2 insertion and Hungarian assignment so neighboring POIs share the same day.
  5. Budget allocation (allocate_trip_budget): Distributes available discretionary budget pro-rata across active days using live FX conversions.
  6. Parallel C++20 daily solving (solve_trip_v2): Flattens each day's Valhalla/transit matrices and invokes paladio_core.optimize_itinerary across threads (asyncio.to_thread with GIL released), returning exact arrival_times.
  7. Budget slack redistribution: Reallocates unspent budget headroom from lighter days to days constrained by paid admissions.
  8. Explainable synthesis: Attaches day themes, selection reason codes, and an explicit list of dropped_pois explaining why omitted venues did not fit.

docs.title: Frontend architecture, PWA offline mode, and Demo branch
docs.text: Built with Next.js 16 (output: 'standalone'), React 19, Vanilla CSS Modules, Leaflet + MapLibre GL, and 7 Zustand stores, the frontend provides a localized multi-theme workspace with IndexedDB offline persistence plus an encrypted standalone demo deployment mode.

docs.title: Pacific Jazz styling, state management, and map stack
docs.text:
Paladio avoids heavy UI component frameworks in favor of CSS custom properties in frontend/src/app/globals.css paired with scoped *.module.css files and zero-flicker head theme hydration in layout.tsx.

  • Design system: Supports 3 themes (Pacific Jazz Light, Pacific Jazz Dark, Silent Waters), 2 typography scales (Inter vs Classic Jost + Inter + JetBrains Mono), and 2 navigation shells (Sidebar vs FloatingDock), plus custom tactical SVG illustrations under frontend/src/components/illustrations/.
  • 7 Zustand stores (frontend/src/stores/): localeStore, themeStore, typographyStore, navigationStore, sidebarStore, notificationStore (100-item per-user inbox), and tripDraftStore (/engine form draft persistence), alongside 3 React contexts (AuthContext, I18nContext, SocketContext).
  • 2D vector + cluster cartography: Combines leaflet + react-leaflet + react-leaflet-cluster with maplibre-gl (VectorBasemap.tsx using public/worker/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs to strip 3D extrusions and visual clutter from OpenFreeMap liberty tiles) and selectable raster basemaps (OSM, Carto Voyager, Carto Dark, Satellite).

docs.title: 10-locale internationalization and RTL layout
docs.text:
Every user-facing string runs through useTranslation() (t(...)), validated across all 10 dictionary files (en, es, fr, de, it, pt, ja, zh-CN, ko, ar) by scripts/i18n/validate_locales.py.

  • en.json ships bundled as the default fallback with an English-to-key reverse fallback map in localeStore.ts; the remaining 9 dictionaries lazy-load from /locales/{code}.json.
  • Selecting Arabic (ar) switches <html dir="rtl"> dynamically across layouts, calendars, and modals.

docs.title: Service Worker and IndexedDB offline trip pinning
docs.text:
For reliable field use without roaming connectivity, PwaRegistration.tsx registers frontend/public/sw.js alongside frontend/src/utils/offlineStore.ts:

  • Service Worker caches: Uses cache-first caching (paladio-shell-v1) for /_next/static/ assets and network-first with cache fallback (paladio-data-v1) for /api/trips and OpenFreeMap/OSM/Carto map tiles.
  • Explicit offline trip pinning: Clicking the header pin icon inside /trips/[id] (pinTripOffline(tripId)) stores the full trip JSON, Wallet passes, raw ticket file attachments, and trip expenses in IndexedDB.

docs.title: How the standalone demo branch works
docs.text:
The public interactive preview lives on a separate demo branch kept automatically synchronized with main by .github/workflows/sync-demo.yml (and guarded locally by scripts/guard_demo_branch.sh in pre-commit).

flowchart LR
    Local["Local Stack + Postgres/GTFS"] -->|"scripts/build_demo_server_snapshot.py"| Enc["demo-snapshot.enc (AES-256-GCM + gzip)"]
    Main["Push to main"] -->|"sync-demo.yml merge & tsc"| DemoBranch["demo branch"]
    DemoBranch -->|"DEMO_DATA_KEY env"| NextAPI["Next.js /api/[...path] route handler"]
    NextAPI --> DemoStore["demoStore + demoHandlers (3 trips, 2 vault, 3 routes)"]
  • On demo, Next.js intercepts /api/* requests through frontend/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts, decrypts frontend/src/server/demo-snapshot.enc with DEMO_DATA_KEY, and serves realistic PostgreSQL-captured trips, GTFS stations, and route telemetry in memory without requiring Docker Postgres, Redis, or Valhalla containers.
  • Writes inside the demo reset cleanly on schedule (DemoResetTimer) while keeping admin secrets and destructive infrastructure routes gated (DemoFeatureGate).

docs.title: Semantic RAG and taste learning engine
docs.text: Paladio embeds POIs and user preferences in-process on CPU via fastembed, retrieves candidates with hybrid SQL Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and Spatial-Semantic Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR), and ranks venues using pure-NumPy Bayesian + online Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) models.

docs.title: In-process CPU ONNX embeddings (OnnxEmbeddingProvider)
docs.text:
Running embeddings through an external Ollama daemon previously added container startup latency, GPU/VRAM contention, and network hop failures. backend/app/infrastructure/providers/onnx_embedding_provider.py embeds text directly inside Python using quantized CPU ONNX (fastembed, model nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5-Q, baked into /opt/models/fastembed during Docker build).

  • 768-dimensional L2-normalized vectors: Applies task-aware search_query: and search_document: prefixes so asymmetrical short queries match rich versioned v3 POI documents built by backend/app/engine/hydration/document_builder.py.
  • Idle RAM reclamation: Honors FASTEMBED_THREADS and optional FASTEMBED_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to release ONNX runtime sessions and trim heap memory (malloc_trim) when idle.
  • Zero-LLM PromptIntentExtractor: Projects user trip prompts against curated 768-D semantic anchor vectors and combines rapidfuzz fuzzy DB matching (backend/app/engine/nlp/intent_extractor.py) to extract mandatory POIs, tastes, cuisines, pace, and offbeat preference without calling a chat LLM.

docs.title: Hybrid SQL RRF retrieval and Spatial-Semantic MMR
docs.text:
HybridRetriever (backend/app/engine/retrieval/hybrid_retriever.py) fuses four PostgreSQL signals inside a single database round-trip before diversifying results geographically:

  1. Vector cosine similarity: pgvector HNSW index (m=16, ef_construction=128) on attractions.embedding.
  2. Full-text search (FTS): PostgreSQL tsvector GIN index over normalized names, descriptions, and facets.
  3. Fuzzy trigram matching: pg_trgm GIN index catching misspellings, accents, and partial venue titles.
  4. Structured JSONB facets: jsonb_path_ops GIN index filtering opening hours, indoor/outdoor traits, and cost brackets extracted by facet_extractor.py.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) merges ranked lists across those signals, and Spatial-Semantic Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) then prevents near-duplicate venues in the same micro-block from crowding out neighborhood variety.

docs.title: 16-D PoiEncoder, HybridSovereignScorer, and online SGD
docs.text:
HybridSovereignScorer (backend/app/infrastructure/scoring/hybrid_scorer.py) completely replaced the legacy untrained JAX/Flax MLP with an interpretable, deterministic pure-NumPy utility function ([0.0, 100.0]) paired with PoiEncoder (backend/app/engine/scoring/features.py, FEATURE_DIM = 16):

Feature index Signal Normalization / representation [0] Admission cost cost / 200.0 clipped to [0.0, 1.0] [1] Visit dwell duration duration_mins / 240.0 clipped to [0.0, 1.0] [2], [4] Rating Normalized rating / 5.0 and raw [0.0, 5.0] [3], [5] Review popularity Normalized log10(reviews + 1) / 5.0 and raw count [6] Free admission flag 1.0 if cost <= 0 else 0.0 [7] Outdoor flag 1.0 if nature_outdoors tag active [8..15] 8 category tag activations art_culture, history_heritage, nature_outdoors, architecture, food_culinary, nightlife, shopping, scenic_views

Default hybrid scorer weights combine quality (w_quality = 0.35, Bayesian smoothed with prior_reviews_m = 50.0 and prior_rating_C = 4.0), tag/semantic affinity (w_affinity = 0.40), pacing fit (w_pacing = 0.15), and budget fit (w_budget = 0.10). Online SGD updates (learning_rate = 0.15, l2_reg = 0.01), TasteService (backend/app/application/taste/taste_service.py), and TasteRankerModel persist implicit and explicit signals (taste_events) into user_taste_profiles, support group consensus merging for multi-traveler trips, and retrain nightly at 04:00 UTC via Celery Beat (retrain_taste_profiles_task).

docs.title: System architecture overview
docs.text: Paladio separates deterministic travel planning, mathematical route optimization, and local semantic search from optional conversational Large Language Model (LLM) interfaces across a 7-container self-hosted stack and a Clean Architecture backend.

docs.title: Why deterministic planning replaces end-to-end LLM chains
docs.text:
Earlier iterations delegated booking parsing, constraint extraction, and route scoring to local LLM calls and an untrained JAX Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), which introduced non-deterministic schedules, latency spikes, and arithmetic errors. Paladio now enforces a strict architectural split:

  • Deterministic generation and optimization: Booking text parsing, constraint assembly, 768-dimensional semantic embedding (fastembed CPU ONNX), multi-attribute ranking (HybridSovereignScorer), and daily itinerary scheduling (paladio_core C++20) run without generative LLM calls.
  • Optional conversational orchestration: Generative LLMs (13 supported providers) are isolated strictly inside TripAgentRunner (backend/app/agent/) for Plan -> Agent chat, calling verified deterministic tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server under strict human-in-the-loop confirmation gates.

docs.title: Clean Architecture backend boundaries
docs.text:
The backend (backend/app/) enforces dependency inversion so domain entities and solvers stay decoupled from FastAPI routers, SQLAlchemy ORM sessions, and external HTTP scrapers.

flowchart TB
    API["app/api & app/agent & app/mcp (Transport)"] --> App["app/application & app/use_cases (Orchestration)"]
    App --> Domain["app/domain (Entities & Port Protocols)"]
    App --> Engine["app/engine (Itinerary v2, Scoring, NLP, Market)"]
    Swarm["app/swarm (9-Node Deterministic Graph)"] --> App
    Adapters["app/adapters & app/infrastructure (SQL, ONNX, Valhalla, Fares)"] --> Domain
    Engine --> CPP["paladio_core (C++20 TCOPTW / TSPTW)"]
Layer Responsibility Key modules Domain Pure entities (City, Poi, Taste), 10 repository/provider port protocols, ISO currency codes backend/app/domain/ Application & Use Cases Trip editing, revision snapshots, expense settlement, participants, tickets, collections, taste service backend/app/application/, backend/app/use_cases/ Core Engine 8-stage Itinerary v2 pipeline, PromptIntentExtractor, SQL RRF retrieval, HybridSovereignScorer, Deal Engine backend/app/engine/ Swarm 9-node deterministic LangGraph state machine with 2 interrupt() human-in-the-loop checkpoints backend/app/swarm/ Adapters & Infrastructure Async SQLAlchemy repositories, OnnxEmbeddingProvider, OSM/PBF/Wikimedia ingest, CppOptimizationAdapter backend/app/adapters/, backend/app/infrastructure/ Transport & Workers 15 FastAPI routers, 2 WebSockets, FastMCP /mcp mount, and 18 Celery tasks across 3 queues backend/app/api/, backend/app/agent/, backend/app/mcp/, backend/app/tasks.py

docs.title: Dynamic data invariant and zero-legacy policy
docs.text:
Two repository-wide engineering invariants shape every subsystem in Paladio:

  1. Dynamic data everywhere: Production paths across the frontend, backend, swarm, and C++ core never emit mock itineraries, synthetic fallback POIs, or hardcoded pricing catalogs. Data is loaded dynamically from PostgreSQL 16 (TimescaleDB + pgvector), OpenStreetMap/Wikidata/Wikimedia, Valhalla/GTFS feeds, live exchange rates, or user input, failing fast when required data is missing.
  2. Zero legacy compatibility shims: Routes, schemas, and storage tables evolve cleanly in place without /api/v1 version aliases, schema synonym fields, or backward-compatibility wrappers (for example, the obsolete city_transit_fares table was dropped outright in favor of the normalized 14-table GTFS + transit_fare_quotes design).

docs.title: Developer guide and contributing conventions
docs.text: Follow Paladio's strict dynamic-data, zero-legacy, and 10-locale internationalization rules, extend backend capabilities cleanly through Clean Architecture ports or FastMCP tools, verify changes with scoped test commands, and synchronize documentation to the GitHub Wiki.

docs.title: Non-negotiable engineering invariants
docs.text:
Contributions across backend/, cpp_core/, and frontend/ must adhere to the repository rules enforced by code review and pre-commit tooling:

  • Dynamic data everywhere: Never introduce mock fallbacks, hardcoded POI fixtures, or static business tables into production paths (backend/app/, frontend/src/, cpp_core/src/). Fail fast when external APIs or database catalogs are missing; isolate test fixtures strictly inside backend/tests/, frontend/tests/, and cpp_core/tests/.
  • Zero-legacy architecture: Do not add /api/v1 route aliases, schema synonym fields, or backward-compatibility wrappers. Refactor callers across frontend, backend, MCP tools, and tests directly into the unified modern contract.
  • Mandatory 10-locale i18n: Wrap every new or modified user-facing string in useTranslation() (t(...)) and add matching translations across all 10 files in frontend/public/locales/ (ar.json, de.json, en.json, es.json, fr.json, it.json, ja.json, ko.json, pt.json, zh-CN.json).
  • DCO 1.1 sign-off and branch protection: Sign every commit (git commit -s). The pre-commit hook runs ruff, ruff-format, eslint, clang-format, and scripts/guard_demo_branch.sh (which blocks accidental direct commits onto demo).

docs.title: Verifying changes with scoped checks
docs.text:
Run pinpoint tests matching the files you modified rather than slow whole-repo verbose runs, and validate all 10 translation files whenever editing UI text.

# 1. C++20 unit & stress tests
cmake -S cpp_core -B cpp_core/build -DPALADIO_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build cpp_core/build -j4 && ctest --test-dir cpp_core/build --output-on-failure

# 2. Scoped backend pytest run
pytest backend/tests/test_bridge.py -k test_bridge_solver -q

# 3. Frontend lint, component tests, and scoped Playwright E2E
cd frontend && npm run lint && npm run test:ct && npx playwright test tests/e2e/engine.spec.ts

# 4. 10-locale translation parity & untranslated string check
python3 scripts/i18n/validate_locales.py
python3 scripts/i18n/find_untranslated.py

docs.title: Common extension recipes
docs.text: Each subsystem isolates extension points so new capabilities inherit authentication, revision snapshots, and strict validation automatically.

docs.title: Adding a new MCP tool and agent toolset entry
docs.text:
1. Implement the async tool function inside the matching module under backend/app/mcp/tools/, validating trip access via get_user_context and assert_trip_access, and returning create_proposal(...) if the operation requires Tier C confirmation.
  2. Export the function in backend/app/mcp/tools/__init__.py.
  3. Register it in backend/app/mcp/server.py with mcp.tool(name=…, description=…, annotations=make_annotations(read_only=…, idempotent=…, destructive=…)).
  4. Add the tool name either to CORE_TOOLS or a domain bucket in DOMAIN_TOOLSETS inside backend/app/agent/toolsets.py so TripAgentRunner discovers it dynamically.

docs.title: Adding a city transit fare adapter
docs.text:
1. Subclass BaseFareAdapter (backend/app/adapters/fares/base_fare_adapter.py) following odpt.py or tfl.py.
  2. Return normalized fare quotes with provenance URLs and evidence_hash digests for FareResolver (backend/app/services/fare_resolver.py) to persist in transit_fare_quotes.

docs.title: Extending paladio_core C++20 constraints
docs.text:
1. Add fields to POI or OptimizationConfig in cpp_core/include/paladio/engine.hpp with clean default values.
  2. Enforce the constraint inside cpp_core/src/engine.cpp without adding heap allocations to SearchState.
  3. Expose matching read/write properties and constructor arguments in cpp_core/src/bindings.cpp, update cpp_core/src/paladio_core.pyi and backend/paladio_core.pyi, and add GoogleTest coverage in cpp_core/tests/cpp/engine_test.cpp.

docs.title: Building docs locally and syncing the GitHub Wiki
docs.text:
mkdocs.yml is the single source of truth for both the GitHub Pages portal (.github/workflows/docs.yml) and the GitHub Wiki (scripts/sync_wiki.py).

  1. Validate the MkDocs site with --strict before committing documentation changes (building into /tmp avoids cluttering the workspace):
.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict -d /tmp/paladio_mkdocs_verify && rm -rf /tmp/paladio_mkdocs_verify
  1. Regenerate and push the synchronized GitHub Wiki (converting admonitions, tabs, relative links, and screenshot URLs while pruning retired wiki pages):
git clone git@github.com:Leandro-Juan/paladio.wiki.git /tmp/paladio_wiki_sync
.venv/bin/python scripts/sync_wiki.py --docs-dir docs --wiki-dir /tmp/paladio_wiki_sync --push
rm -rf /tmp/paladio_wiki_sync

docs.title: Install Paladio with Docker
docs.text: Deploy the full 7-container Paladio stack (api, frontend, db, redis, valhalla, worker, beat) using Docker Compose, generate bootstrap secrets in .env, verify GET /health, and provision your first administrator account at /setup.

docs.title: Prerequisites and hardware sizing
docs.text:
Paladio runs locally on Linux, macOS, or Windows with Docker Engine and Docker Compose v2 installed, and needs enough RAM to keep PostgreSQL, Valhalla street graphs, and CPU ONNX embeddings responsive concurrently.

Resource Minimum Recommended Why it matters RAM 8 GB 12 GB to 16 GB valhalla reserves up to 3,072 MB (mem_limit: 3072m), api and worker allow up to 2,048 MB each, and beat allows 512 MB CPU 4 cores 6+ cores In-process CPU ONNX inference (FASTEMBED_THREADS=2), C++20 paladio_core compilation, and Valhalla routing tiles (cpus: 2.0) Disk 20 GB free 50 GB+ free Docker images, /opt/models/fastembed ONNX weights, pgdata, valhalladata OSM extracts, and gtfsdata transit feeds Software Docker + Compose v2 Docker Engine 24+ scripts/install/install.sh and scripts/install/install.ps1 abort if docker, the Docker daemon, or docker compose version is unavailable

docs.title: Services and persistent volumes
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml defines seven coordinated services and four named volumes so your trips, wallet attachments, OSM tiles, and GTFS feeds survive container upgrades.

Service Role Host port binding Named volumes api FastAPI gateway, WebSockets, MCP /mcp server ${API_PORT:-8000}:8000 valhalladata, gtfsdata, ./backend:/app, /var/run/docker.sock frontend Next.js 16 standalone web UI ${FRONTEND_PORT:-3000}:3000 None db PostgreSQL 16 (timescale/timescaledb:latest-pg16) + pgvector 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 pgdata redis Celery broker, pub/sub events, turn locks, caches 127.0.0.1:6379:6379 redisdata valhalla Self-hosted OSM road, foot, bike, and transit graph router 127.0.0.1:8002:8002 valhalladata, gtfsdata worker Celery worker (celery, transit_build, poi_hydration queues) None valhalladata, gtfsdata, ./backend:/app, /var/run/docker.sock beat Celery Beat scheduler (market sweeps, taste retraining, update checks) None ./backend:/app

Docker socket mount on api and worker

Both api and worker mount /var/run/docker.sock so the transit pipeline can signal or restart the valhalla container after compiling new city map extracts or GTFS feeds. Only run Paladio on trusted host infrastructure.

docs.title: Install from a cloned repository
docs.text:
Cloning the repository is the supported installation path because docker-compose.yml currently builds backend/Dockerfile (target: dev) and frontend/Dockerfile from your local workspace.

  1. Clone the repository and enter the project directory:
git clone https://github.com/Leandro-Juan/paladio.git
cd paladio
  1. Run the bootstrap installer or create .env from .env.example to generate a random POSTGRES_PASSWORD and JWT_SECRET_KEY:
Linux / macOS (automated)Windows PowerShell (automated)Manual .env setup 
./scripts/install/install.sh

.\scripts\install\install.ps1

cp .env.example .env
# Replace POSTGRES_PASSWORD and JWT_SECRET_KEY with random secrets:
openssl rand -hex 32
docker compose up -d --build
  1. Confirm the backend gateway is serving health checks and verify database migrations are applied:
curl -fs http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
docker compose exec api alembic upgrade head
  1. Seed the verified global transit fare quotes if your database starts empty:
docker compose exec api python scripts/migrate_verified_fares_to_quotes.py

About the one-line remote installer scripts

scripts/install/install.sh and scripts/install/install.ps1 support piping directly from GitHub (curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Leandro-Juan/paladio/main/scripts/install/install.sh | bash), which downloads docker-compose.yml into $HOME/paladio. Because the current docker-compose.yml references local build: contexts (backend/Dockerfile and frontend/Dockerfile) instead of prebuilt GitHub Container Registry images (ghcr.io/leandro-juan/paladio-api and ghcr.io/leandro-juan/paladio-frontend), always clone the repository first before running ./scripts/install/install.sh or .\scripts\install\install.ps1.

docs.title: First-run administrator provisioning
docs.text:
When you open http://localhost:3000 on a fresh database with zero user accounts, AuthGuard queries GET /api/auth/setup-status and routes you automatically to /setup.

  1. Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser and wait for the backend auto-reconnect check to finish if api is still starting.
  2. Enter your administrator Username, Email, and Password (minimum 6 characters) on /setup and submit the form (POST /api/auth/setup).
  3. Paladio signs you in with an HS256 JWT token valid for ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES (default 1440, or 24 hours) and redirects you to Control Center (/dashboard).

Public registration is disabled by default

After the first admin account exists, /register and POST /api/auth/register stay locked unless you set ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION=true in the environment. Administrators can provision additional user accounts inside Settings (/config under Authorized Users).

docs.title: Troubleshooting installation startup
docs.text:
If containers fail to start or /health times out after 60s, inspect service logs to isolate build, memory, or port conflicts:

docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f --tail=100 api worker db valhalla
  • Port 3000 or 8000 already in use: Set API_PORT or FRONTEND_PORT in .env and restart with docker compose up -d.
  • Missing pgvector or timescaledb extension: Verify the db service uses timescale/timescaledb:latest-pg16 and run docker compose exec db psql -U postgres -d paladio -c "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;".
  • Out-of-memory kills during first build: Ensure Docker Desktop or your Linux VM has at least 8 GB of RAM assigned before building cpp_core and downloading nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5-Q into /opt/models/fastembed.

Next, complete your initial taste profile and generate your first deterministic itinerary in Quickstart: plan your first trip.

docs.title: Local development setup
docs.text: Build the cpp_core C++20 extension, run the FastAPI gateway and Celery workers in Python 3.12+, start the Next.js 16 development server, and execute targeted component and end-to-end test suites outside Docker.

docs.title: Build and test the C++20 core (cpp_core)
docs.text:
cpp_core/ has zero third-party C++ runtime dependencies and uses CMake 3.20+ with FetchContent to download pybind11 v2.11.1 and GoogleTest v1.14.0 during configuration. Compiler warnings are treated as errors (-Wall -Wextra -Werror).

  1. Configure and compile the static library (paladio_engine_static), pybind11 module (paladio_core), and C++ unit tests:
cmake -S cpp_core -B cpp_core/build -DPALADIO_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build cpp_core/build -j4
  1. Run the 23 GoogleTest cases via CTest:
ctest --test-dir cpp_core/build --output-on-failure
  1. Build with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer when debugging memory or bitmask logic:
cmake -S cpp_core -B cpp_core/build-asan \
  -DPALADIO_BUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DPALADIO_ENABLE_SANITIZERS=ON
cmake --build cpp_core/build-asan -j4
ctest --test-dir cpp_core/build-asan --output-on-failure
  1. Install paladio_core into your active Python virtual environment via scikit-build-core:
pip install -e ./cpp_core --no-build-isolation
pytest cpp_core/tests/python/test_engine.py -q

Standalone paladio_core build flags

Pass -DPALADIO_ENABLE_NATIVE=ON in Release builds to add -march=native alongside -O3 -DNDEBUG, or -DPALADIO_BUILD_PYTHON=OFF when embedding only the paladio::engine C++ static target.

docs.title: Run the FastAPI backend and Celery workers
docs.text:
The backend requires Python 3.10+ (Docker uses Python 3.12), PostgreSQL 16 with timescaledb and vector extensions, Redis 7, Valhalla (optional for local unit tests), Tesseract OCR, and Poppler utilities.

  1. Install OS packages required for boarding pass and receipt OCR on Debian/Ubuntu:
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y \
  tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng tesseract-ocr-spa poppler-utils fonts-liberation
  1. Create a Python virtual environment, install backend with dev extras, and ensure paladio_core*.so is importable in backend/:
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e "./backend[dev]"
  1. Start PostgreSQL, Redis, and Valhalla via Docker Compose while running Python processes natively on your host, then apply Alembic migrations and verified fare quotes:
docker compose up -d db redis valhalla
cd backend
alembic upgrade head
python scripts/migrate_verified_fares_to_quotes.py
  1. Launch FastAPI, the Celery worker across all three queues (celery, transit_build, poi_hydration), and Celery Beat in separate terminals:
uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload --reload-dir app

celery -A app.celery_app worker --loglevel=info \
  -Q celery,transit_build,poi_hydration -c 2 --prefetch-multiplier=1

celery -A app.celery_app beat --loglevel=info
  1. Run targeted backend tests (backend/tests/conftest.py installs a Python fallback mock only if compiled paladio_core is missing, so test with compiled paladio_core whenever verifying solver output):
pytest backend/tests/test_bridge.py -k test_bridge_solver -q

Optional Playwright scraping dependency

playwright is intentionally omitted from backend/pyproject.toml and backend/Dockerfile, and is lazy-imported only when optional browser-based lodging or rating enrichment fallbacks run (booking_scraper.py, google_maps_rating_resolver.py, cli/enrich_ratings.py).

docs.title: Run the Next.js 16 frontend and Playwright suites
docs.text:
The frontend uses Node.js 22, Next.js 16 (^16.4.6), React 19 (19.2.8), CSS Modules, and Playwright for both React component testing and full end-to-end tests.

  1. Install dependencies and start the development server:
cd frontend
npm ci
npm run dev
  1. Run ESLint, Playwright component tests (playwright-ct.config.ts), or a scoped E2E test (playwright.config.ts):
npm run lint
npm run test:ct
npx playwright test tests/e2e/engine.spec.ts
  1. Install pre-commit hooks from the repository root so ruff, ruff-format, eslint, clang-format, and scripts/guard_demo_branch.sh run before every commit:
pre-commit install

docs.title: Quickstart: plan your first trip
docs.text: Sign into your new Paladio instance, initialize your 8-axis Taste Star profile at /taste-calibration, and generate your first deterministic itinerary in New Trip (/engine) without needing any external generative AI key.

docs.title: Calibrate your 8-axis Taste Star
docs.text:
New accounts start with a neutral taste vector (0.5 across all dimensions), which displays a calibration banner on Control Center (/dashboard). Completing /taste-calibration seeds your personal 768-dimensional preference profile for Point of Interest (POI) matching before you generate a trip.

  1. Click the Seed Your Taste banner on /dashboard (or navigate to http://localhost:3000/taste-calibration).
  2. Answer the 8 scenario questions (first_morning, afternoon_pace, urban_form, dining_style, after_sunset, markets_craft, budget_strategy, and crowd_discovery) or skip any question you want to leave neutral.
  3. Submit your answers to update your UserTasteProfileModel and view your updated Taste Star radar (art_culture, history_heritage, nature_outdoors, architecture, food_culinary, nightlife, shopping, and scenic_views) on /dashboard.

docs.title: Create a personalized trip in /engine
docs.text:
Opening New Trip (/engine) lets you choose between Personalized Trip (runs the deterministic LangGraph swarm and paladio_core C++20 optimizer) and Blank Trip (opens an empty workspace for manual curation).

  1. Select Personalized Trip in the mode toggle at the top of /engine.
  2. Fill in your ORIG and DEST city/airport codes and arrival/departure hours in the route intake bar so Day 1 and the final day respect airport transfer windows.
  3. Select your travel dates in the date range picker, set your hotel stay anchor (either by hotel search or by dropping a map pin), and enter your target budget with the currency wheel picker.
  4. Optionally add fellow travelers in the Crew Roster or upload flight and hotel confirmation files (PDF, PNG, JPG, WEBP, TXT, .pkpass, or .trip) via the upload modal for automatic local parsing.
  5. Describe your preferences in the intent box (for example, Quiet museums, historic neighborhoods, specialty coffee, and late tapas) and click Generate Sovereign Trip Plan.

docs.title: Review live swarm telemetry and verification checkpoints
docs.text:
Paladio connects over WS /api/ws/stream and streams real-time progress through the ThinkingScreen while the 9-node deterministic swarm hydrates city POIs and computes travel matrices.

  1. When the Verification Required modal appears (verify_constraints human-in-the-loop checkpoint), confirm the extracted origin, destination, dates, budget, and hotel anchor, or adjust any field before proceeding.
  2. If your new dates overlap an existing trip in PostgreSQL, resolve or acknowledge the Trip Overlap Warning modal (guardrails checkpoint).
  3. Wait for planner_scrape, planner_optimize (paladio_core.optimize_itinerary), planner_critic, and planner_repair to complete and redirect you automatically to /trips/[id].

Zero LLM keys required for trip generation

All 9 swarm nodes (ticket_parser, assemble_constraints, verify_constraints, guardrails, prompt_analyzer, planner_scrape, planner_optimize, planner_critic, planner_repair) execute deterministically using regex parsers, CPU ONNX embeddings, and C++20 branch-and-bound search. Generative LLM API keys are needed only if you later enable the optional interactive chat assistant inside Plan -> Agent.

docs.title: Inspect and refine your generated itinerary
docs.text:
Your trip opens in the full-screen Trip Workspace (/trips/[id]), pairing an interactive 2D architectural map on the right with a 6-tab sidebar on the left (Route, Search, Transit, Weather, Collections, Agent).

  1. Switch between ALL DAYS and individual day pills (DAY 1, DAY 2, …) in the Route tab to inspect stop times, meal windows, and walking or transit leg connectors.
  2. Click the bottom-left Speed Dial (+) button and toggle EDIT ROUTE to lock fixed-time reservations, drag stops to reorder a day, or delete stops.
  3. Click Solve to re-run the C++20 Time-Constrained Orienteering Problem with Time Windows (TCOPTW) / TSPTW solver around your locked anchors.

Next, learn every panel of the workspace in Control Center and Taste Star and Trip Workspace and editing.

docs.title: C++20 and Python API reference (paladio_core)
docs.text: paladio_core exposes paladio::core (cpp_core/include/paladio/engine.hpp) to Python via pybind11 (cpp_core/src/bindings.cpp, typed in cpp_core/src/paladio_core.pyi), releasing the Python Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) across all three combinatorial solvers.

docs.title: Build options and packaging
docs.text:
cpp_core/CMakeLists.txt (PaladioEngine v2.0.0) compiles pure C++20 (-Wall -Wextra -Werror) into paladio_engine_static (paladio::engine) and the paladio_core Python extension module, while cpp_core/pyproject.toml builds PEP 517 Python wheels through scikit-build-core (numpy>=1.20.0).

CMake option Default Purpose PALADIO_BUILD_TESTS OFF Fetches GoogleTest v1.14.0 and builds the 23 C++ tests (paladio_tests) PALADIO_ENABLE_NATIVE OFF Adds -march=native alongside -O3 -DNDEBUG in Release builds PALADIO_ENABLE_SANITIZERS OFF Adds -g -Og -fsanitize=address,undefined to compile and link flags PALADIO_BUILD_PYTHON ON Fetches pybind11 v2.11.1 and builds paladio_core + installs paladio_core.pyi and py.typed

docs.title: NodeType enumeration
docs.text:
paladio_core.NodeType (enum class NodeType : uint8_t) classifies vertices for meal fulfillment, active fatigue resets, and monotony grouping; bindings.cpp calls .export_values() so members are accessible both as NodeType.ATTRACTION and directly on paladio_core.

Member Behavioral role in optimize_itinerary ATTRACTION Accrues objective score; subject to time windows, fatigue multiplier, and monotony decay HOTEL Rest depot; resets continuous_active_time to 0 and incurs 0 dwell cost or duration when used as terminal depot RESTAURANT_BREAKFAST Rest node; sets is_breakfast_spot=True, satisfies breakfast_deadline, enforces min_meal_spacing RESTAURANT_LUNCH Rest node; sets is_lunch_spot=True, satisfies lunch_deadline, enforces min_meal_spacing RESTAURANT_DINNER Rest node; sets is_dinner_spot=True, satisfies dinner_deadline, enforces min_meal_spacing BAR Rest node; resets continuous_active_time to 0 without triggering meal spacing

docs.title: POI and TransitInfo structures
docs.text:
Construct POI vertices with operating windows in minutes from midnight (0 to 1440) and non-negative monetary cost, score, and duration. TransitInfo (int duration, double cost) exists only in the C++ #ifdef PALADIO_TESTING convenience overload and is not bound in Python (bindings.cpp).

POI(
    type: NodeType,
    cost: float,
    score: float,
    earliest_time: int,
    latest_time: int,
    duration: int,
    is_mandatory: bool = False,
    category_id: int = 255,
)
Field Type Default / invariant Notes type NodeType Required Drives meal flags (is_breakfast_spot, is_lunch_spot, is_dinner_spot) on construction cost float Required (>= 0.0) Direct visit cost in currency units score float Required (>= 0.0) Base objective utility to maximize earliest_time, latest_time int Required (0 <= earliest <= latest) Arrival + duration must finish at or before latest_time duration int Required (>= 0) Mandatory dwell time in minutes is_breakfast_spot, is_lunch_spot, is_dinner_spot bool Derived from type Readable/writable in Python to mark mixed venues or hotels is_mandatory bool False Candidate paths omitting mandatory vertices are pruned category_id int (uint8_t) 255 Taxonomy slot 0–15 for monotony decay; 255 falls back to NodeType

docs.title: OptimizationConfig and OptimizationResult
docs.text:
OptimizationConfig bundles hard combinatorial bounds, human-realism physiology rules, and search termination caps; optimize_itinerary returns OptimizationResult (read/write attributes only, no Python __init__).

OptimizationConfig parameter Type Default Description max_budget float Required Upper bound on visit costs plus transit fares start_node_index Optional[int] None Fixed start index (0..N-1); None searches all root candidates end_node_type Optional[NodeType] None Required categorical type for the terminal stop end_node_index Optional[int] None Required terminal node index (for hotel round-trips) end_time_limit int -1 Global itinerary deadline in minutes from midnight (-1 disables) breakfast_deadline, lunch_deadline, dinner_deadline int -1 Latest arrival minute for each meal type (-1 disables) max_idle_time int 60 Maximum allowed waiting minutes before a POI opens idle_time_penalty_rate float 0.5 Score deducted per 15 minutes of idle waiting max_active_time_before_fatigue int 240 Active minutes allowed before fatigue multiplier activates fatigue_penalty_multiplier float 0.6 Score multiplier applied when fatigued (0.0 < mult <= 1.0) min_meal_spacing int 180 Minimum minutes required between consecutive meals monotony_threshold int 2 Category visits allowed before exponential diminishing returns monotony_multiplier float 0.5 Exponential penalty factor mult ** (count - threshold + 1) timeout_ms int 5000 Wall-clock search cap in ms (polled every 1,024 node expansions) max_nodes_expanded int 0 Expansion cap (0 disables limit) OptimizationResult attribute Type Description path list[int] Ordered visited node indices from start to terminal (empty if infeasible) arrival_times list[int] Arrival timestamps in minutes from midnight for each node in path total_cost, total_time, total_score float Total expenditure, elapsed minutes, and net utility score nodes_expanded int Count of branch-and-bound search nodes evaluated timed_out bool True when timeout_ms or max_nodes_expanded halted search with best incumbent

docs.title: Solver entry points (GIL-released)
docs.text:
All three Python functions release the GIL (py::gil_scoped_release), consume 1D row-major N x N NumPy arrays (int32 for durations/windows/dwells, float64 for costs), and raise ValueError (std::invalid_argument in C++) on dimension mismatches or out-of-range depot indices.

optimize_itinerary(
    pois: list[POI],
    durations: npt.NDArray[np.int32],  # flattened N*N, positional-only in Python
    costs: npt.NDArray[np.float64],    # flattened N*N, positional-only in Python
    config: OptimizationConfig,
) -> OptimizationResult

solve_tsp_tour(
    durations: npt.NDArray[np.int32],  # flattened n*n
    n: int,
    start_node: int = 0,
    end_node: int = -1,
    fixed_end: bool = False,
) -> list[int]

solve_tsptw(
    durations: npt.NDArray[np.int32],      # flattened n*n
    n: int,
    dwell_times: npt.NDArray[np.int32],    # length n
    window_starts: npt.NDArray[np.int32],  # length n
    window_ends: npt.NDArray[np.int32],    # length n
    start_node: int = 0,
    end_node: int = -1,
    fixed_end: bool = False,
    penalty_weight: float = 100.0,
) -> list[int]
  • optimize_itinerary arguments are positional-only in bindings.cpp and enforce len(pois) <= 64.
  • solve_tsp_tour and solve_tsptw accept arbitrary n without the 64-node bitmask ceiling and support named keyword arguments in Python.

docs.title: Authentication and authorization model
docs.text:
Protected endpoints require Authorization: Bearer your_jwt_access_token_here signed with HS256 (JWT_SECRET_KEY).

  • Public bootstrap: GET /health, GET /api/auth/setup-status, POST /api/auth/setup (valid only when zero users exist), POST /api/auth/login, and POST /api/auth/register (auto-admin if zero users exist; otherwise gated by ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION).
  • Role tiers: Standard users hold get_current_user; system infrastructure routes enforce get_current_admin_user (role == "admin").
  • Trip RBAC: Trip routes check assert_trip_access(user, trip_id, required_level, db) (VIEWER < EDITOR < OWNER). Unowned local trips (user_id IS NULL) allow owner access in sovereign single-user setups.

docs.title: .trip file package format specification
docs.text: Paladio exports and imports entire expeditions as self-contained .trip ZIP containers (application/vnd.paladio.trip+zip, schema version 1.0.0), supporting both complete private backups (full_vault) and anonymized shareable archives (community_shareable).

docs.title: ZIP container structure and entry order
docs.text:
TripPackager (backend/app/trip_package/packager.py) writes an OpenDocument-style container where mimetype acts as a magic header validated before extracting any payload.

expedition.trip (ZIP container)
├── mimetype                     # MUST be entry #0, ZIP_STORED (uncompressed): application/vnd.paladio.trip+zip
├── paladio.json                 # Root TripPackageManifest with SHA-256 digests and byte sizes
├── itinerary.json               # TripItineraryPackage (days, routes, travel_constraints)
├── wallet.json                  # TripWalletPackage (tickets, booking_anchors, attachment manifest)
├── expenses.json                # TripExpensePackage (currency, participants, expenses, settlement)
├── collections.json             # TripCollectionPackage (curated POI lists, notes)
└── attachments/
    ├── tickets/<id>_<filename>  # Included ONLY in full_vault profile
    └── photos/<photo_filename>  # High-res trip gallery images (when include_photos=True)

docs.title: Export profiles: full_vault versus community_shareable
docs.text:
Choosing export_profile="community_shareable" runs TripSanitizer.sanitize_for_sharing (backend/app/trip_package/sanitizer.py) before sealing the ZIP archive so personal financial records and travel credentials never leak into shared files.

Archive member full_vault behavior community_shareable behavior itinerary.json Preserved intact (days, stops, routes, constraints) Preserved intact wallet.json Preserves all ticket fields and attachments manifest Scrubs reference_code, barcode_payload, holder_name, raw_barcode, attachments, and empties wallet.attachments attachments/tickets/* Packaged from WALLET_STORAGE_DIR and hashed Omitted from archive completely expenses.json Preserves real participant names/emails, expenses, and currency Empties expenses and settlement; anonymizes participants to traveler-1 (Traveler 1), traveler-2, … collections.json & attachments/photos/* Preserved intact Preserved intact (include_photos controllable)

docs.title: Integrity validation, security checks, and endpoints
docs.text:
Before hydrating any .trip upload (POST /api/trips/import or exported via GET /api/trips/{trip_id}/export), TripUnpacker (backend/app/trip_package/unpacker.py) enforces four structural defenses:

  1. MIME verification: Confirms entry 0 is named mimetype, uses ZIP_STORED (uncompressed), and matches application/vnd.paladio.trip+zip verbatim.
  2. SHA-256 checksum validation: Re-hashes every entry listed in paladio.json file_manifest, raising TripPackageValidationError on missing files or digest mismatches.
  3. Pydantic validation: Validates itinerary.json, wallet.json, expenses.json, and collections.json against TripItineraryPackage, TripWalletPackage, TripExpensePackage, and TripCollectionPackage.
  4. Zip-slip path traversal prevention: Resolves each member destination against extract_to_dir.resolve() and aborts if any path escapes the extraction root.

docs.title: WebSocket protocols reference
docs.text: Paladio uses two WebSocket channels for real-time telemetry: /api/ws/stream drives deterministic trip generation and Redis event fan-out, and /api/ws/trip-agent/{trip_id} streams interactive AI assistant turns, proposals, and live trip sync updates.

docs.title: Swarm stream (WS /api/ws/stream)
docs.text: Handled by backend/app/api/websockets.py (SwarmSessionAdapter + SwarmSessionManager), /api/ws/stream accepts optional JWT authentication via ?token=your_jwt_here or inside the JSON payload "token" field, sends a 15s heartbeat ({"event": "HEARTBEAT", "status": "ping"}), and subscribes to the global Redis paladio:events pub/sub channel.

docs.title: Client-to-server actions on /api/ws/stream
docs.text:
Send JSON frames specifying "action" and "thread_id" (a UUID string identifying the LangGraph checkpointer thread). Starting a new action cancels any prior in-flight inference task on the same socket.

Action Key payload fields Purpose "chat" (default) message, prompt, origin_city, destination_city, origin_iata, destination_iata, start_date, end_date, departure_hour, arrival_hour, budget_usd, hotel, participants, scanned_documents, booking_text, booking_anchors, manual_constraints, auto_verify Starts deterministic 9-node trip generation "resume" thread_id, edited verification fields or overlap confirmation fields (Command(resume=data)) Resumes a graph paused at VERIFICATION_REQUIRED or TRIP_OVERLAP_WARNING "feedback" poi, target_score, trip_id Encodes a 16-D POI vector, updates HybridSovereignScorer + 768-D profile, and records a TasteEvent

docs.title: Server-to-client events on /api/ws/stream
docs.text:
Every outbound JSON frame contains "event", "status", and optionally "data" and "thread_id".

Event Trigger UI meaning HEARTBEAT Every 15s Keepalive ping STARTING_INFERENCE / PARSING_TICKETS Swarm start / ticket_parser Generation initialized and booking text parsed EXTRACTING_CONSTRAINTS / VERIFYING_CONSTRAINTS / VERIFICATION_COMPLETED Constraint builder and verification node Constraints assembled or verified VERIFICATION_REQUIRED verify_constraints interrupt() Pauses (status: "awaiting_input") for user constraint confirmation TRIP_OVERLAP_WARNING guardrails date collision interrupt() Pauses (status: "warning") for overlap confirmation GUARDRAILS_ABORTED / GUARDRAILS_PASSED guardrails validation Aborts invalid trip requests or advances to prompt_analyzer ANALYZING_PROMPT prompt_analyzer Deterministic ONNX intent extraction and taste merging SCRAPING_DYNAMIC_DATA planner_scrape Hydrating destination POIs, ratings, and embeddings EVALUATING_ROUTES planner_optimize, planner_critic, planner_repair C++20 TCOPTW solving and critic-repair loop FEEDBACK_PROCESSED "feedback" action Taste vector updated and persisted DONE / ERROR / CLARIFICATION_NEEDED Terminal states Stream finished or failed (status holds error text on failure)

docs.title: Interactive Trip Agent stream (WS /api/ws/trip-agent/{trip_id})
docs.text: Defined in backend/app/agent/api.py, this channel enforces strict JWT authentication (from ?token=, Authorization: Bearer, paladio_token cookie, or access_token cookie) plus assert_trip_access(user, trip_id, TripAccessLevel.VIEWER, db). Connections failing auth close immediately with WS_1008_POLICY_VIOLATION, and connected sockets subscribe to paladio:trip:{trip_id} for external edit broadcasts.

docs.title: Client-to-server AgentClientMessage frames
docs.text:
Every inbound JSON message validates against AgentClientMessage (backend/app/agent/events.py).

type Additional fields Behavior "user_message" message, optional ui_context (tab, day, stop ID, viewport bounds) Starts an exclusive TripAgentRunner turn (90s Redis lock) "approve" proposal_id Re-executes the stored Tier C MCP tool with confirmed=True and consumes the proposal "reject" proposal_id Discards the pending Redis proposal and emits a warning confirmation "cancel" None Triggers the active asyncio.Event cancellation token for trip_id "undo" Optional revision Calls TripService.undo_to_revision or TripService.undo_last_change

docs.title: Server-to-client AgentServerEvent frames
docs.text:
Every outbound JSON frame serializes AgentServerEvent (event, turn_id, timestamp, plus event-specific fields).

event Payload fields Purpose "turn_started" turn_id Signals agent turn start "token" token Streams partial assistant response tokens "tool_call" call_id, tool, args Reports tool invocation start "tool_result" tool, ok, summary, change_set, data Delivers structured tool execution output "proposal" proposal_id, tool, summary, diff, expires_in_seconds (600) Requests user confirmation for a Tier C operation "trip_updated" revision, undo_token, affected_days, changed_stop_ids, summary Broadcasts persisted DB changes (including paladio:trip:{trip_id} updates) "warning" / "error" message, code Emits turn conflicts, cancellations, expired proposals, or failures (BAD_REQUEST, EXPIRED, TURN_FAILED, APPROVAL_FAILED, UNDO_FAILED) "turn_done" final_text, tools_called Marks turn completion

docs.title: Backups, updates, and troubleshooting
docs.text: Protect PostgreSQL data and uploaded attachments with repeatable backup commands, track new releases via the GitHub Auto-Updater, purge stale caches safely, and resolve the most common self-hosted operational failures.

docs.title: Backing up PostgreSQL, volumes, and .trip archives
docs.text:
Back up the PostgreSQL database (pgdata), photo uploads (PHOTO_STORAGE_DIR), wallet attachments (WALLET_STORAGE_DIR), and .env secrets before any major upgrade.

  1. Dump the PostgreSQL 16 + TimescaleDB + pgvector database to a compressed archive:
docker compose exec -T db pg_dump -U postgres -Fc paladio > paladio_$(date +%Y%m%d).dump
  1. Archive user-uploaded photos and encrypted wallet ticket attachments from the api container (skipping valhalladata and gtfsdata if desired because both can be re-derived from OSM and GTFS):
docker compose exec -T api tar -czf - data/trip_photos data/wallet_attachments > paladio_media_$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz
  1. Restore a database dump into a fresh db container:
docker compose exec -T db pg_restore -U postgres -d paladio --clean --if-exists < paladio_20261122.dump
  1. Use Settings -> Data Vault & Backups -> Storage & Snapshots to trigger manual vault snapshots (POST /api/system/vault/snapshot), configure retention (7, 14, 30, or 90 days), or export individual expeditions as Full Vault .trip files for portable per-trip backups.

docs.title: Checking and applying updates
docs.text:
Celery Beat checks GitHub releases every 6 hours (periodic_autoupdate_check_task) and reports release notes in Settings (/config under System Updates).

  • In-app release check: Open Settings -> System Updates to toggle auto-update checks, inspect changelog notes, or download updates (POST /api/system/update/check and /api/system/update/download).
  • Docker Compose upgrade: Pull the latest git commits, back up your database first, rebuild changed images, and apply Alembic migrations:
git pull origin main
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose exec api alembic upgrade head

docs.title: Troubleshooting common self-hosted issues
docs.text:
Check container status and recent logs first whenever a route generation, transit build, or login check stalls:

docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f --tail=100 api worker beat valhalla
Symptom Root cause Resolution Login screen hangs on "Reconnecting…" api is starting, migrating, or failing DB connection Inspect docker compose logs api and verify db health with docker compose exec db pg_isready -U postgres GTFS compile stays stuck in BUILDING Previous worker died while holding paladio:transit_compiler_lock Restart worker (docker compose restart worker) so on_worker_ready clears stale locks and dispatches reconcile_interrupted_transit_builds Missing or broken POI photos / descriptions Corrupted Wikimedia cache entry in Redis or Postgres Run docker compose exec api python scripts/cleanup_corrupted_poi_data.py or trigger Purge System Cache (POST /api/system/cache/purge) in /config Boarding pass PDF scan returns empty fields Host running outside Docker without OCR binaries Install tesseract-ocr, tesseract-ocr-eng, tesseract-ocr-spa, and poppler-utils on the host Valhalla container exits with OOM (137) Large regional OSM extract exceeds mem_limit: 3072m Increase valhalla mem_limit in docker-compose.yml or delete unused city extracts under Settings -> City Data Interactive Agent returns Model too large or OOM on Ollama HardwareService detected insufficient free RAM/VRAM Switch to a smaller quantized model (for example qwen2.5:3b) or click Unload Model in Settings -> AI & LLM Engine WebSocket disconnects immediately behind proxy Reverse proxy drops Upgrade: websocket or times out idle frames Add WebSocket Upgrade/Connection headers and increase proxy_read_timeout as shown in Reverse proxy and security

docs.title: Managing city POIs, Valhalla maps, and GTFS
docs.text: Hydrate destination Point of Interest (POI) catalogs, download OpenStreetMap extracts for Valhalla street routing, compile open General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) schedules into 14 PostgreSQL tables, and inspect storage footprints inside Settings (/config under City Data).

docs.title: How city storage is organized
docs.text:
Every destination stored in Paladio spans three complementary local datasets so itinerary generation, walking legs, and transit routing stay fast and self-contained.

Dataset Storage location Celery queue How it is refreshed POIs & 768-D embeddings PostgreSQL cities + attractions (Vector(768) HNSW index) poi_hydration 3-stage pipeline: ingest_city_pois_task, enrich_tier12_city_pois_task, enrich_long_tail_city_pois_task Street & walk graph Docker volume valhalladata (/custom_files) transit_build build_city_map_task downloads regional OSM PBF extracts and triggers Valhalla tile reloads Compiled transit schedules Docker volume gtfsdata (/gtfs_feeds) + 14 transit_* PostgreSQL tables transit_build build_city_gtfs_task followed by derive_city_transit_task

docs.title: Managing cities from Settings (/config)
docs.text:
Open Settings (/config), select Travel Engine & Optimization -> City Data, and inspect the storage vault table listing every hydrated or planned city.

  1. Click Sync Planned Trips GTFS (POST /api/trips/transit/sync-planned) to verify every upcoming expedition and enqueue GTFS compilation for missing destination cities automatically.
  2. Trigger Download POIs or Compile GTFS on an individual city row when pre-warming a new destination before building a trip.
  3. Click Delete POIs (DELETE /api/trips/city/{city}/pois) or Delete GTFS (DELETE /api/trips/transit/{city}) to reclaim PostgreSQL rows and disk space after completing an expedition.

Single-city compiler lock and crash recovery

To prevent RAM spikes from concurrent Valhalla tile builds, build_city_gtfs_task acquires a distributed Redis lock (paladio:transit_compiler_lock) and processes queued cities sequentially. When a worker starts or recovers from a container restart, on_worker_ready clears stale locks and dispatches reconcile_interrupted_transit_builds to resume interrupted BUILDING or QUEUED jobs automatically.

docs.title: Running operational maintenance scripts and CLIs
docs.text:
When bootstrapping cities offline, troubleshooting corrupted cache entries, or auditing database quality, execute Paladio's built-in administrative commands inside the api container.

Command Module / Script Purpose Hydrate city POIs from CLI python -m app.cli.hydrate_pois Hydrate and embed POIs for target cities directly Enrich POI tiers & ratings python -m app.cli.enrich_pois / tier_pois Run Wikidata, Wikivoyage, and tier classification passes Derive GTFS PostgreSQL tables python -m app.cli.derive_transit Rebuild the 14 derived transit_* tables from a GTFS archive Probe city coverage & quality python -m app.cli.city_quality_probe Inspect POI density, opening hours, and embedding readiness Clean corrupted POI data python scripts/cleanup_corrupted_poi_data.py Flush corrupted Redis Wikimedia caches and reset affected POI descriptions Reseed verified fare quotes python scripts/migrate_verified_fares_to_quotes.py Populate transit_fare_quotes with cited official fares

Execute any script cleanly through Docker Compose:

docker compose exec api python scripts/cleanup_corrupted_poi_data.py

If a city lacks an open GTFS feed in the global catalog, Paladio logs the UNAVAILABLE status in transit_coverage and automatically falls back to Valhalla street walking/driving plus Transitous live transit queries without blocking itinerary generation.

docs.title: Configuration and environment variables
docs.text: Paladio splits configuration cleanly between static bootstrap credentials in .env (for PostgreSQL, JWT signing, wallet encryption, and container networking) and dynamic runtime settings stored in PostgreSQL system_config via Settings (/config).

docs.title: How .env and /config work together
docs.text:
Keep root infrastructure secrets in .env, then manage solvers, LLM providers, backups, photo sync, notifications, and Travelpayouts keys directly inside /config so changes take effect without editing compose manifests.

Settings category in /config Sections included Access level Workspace & Experience Personal Account (profile, avatar, password, language, base currency, units, clock, date format, holiday country) and Appearance & Interface (3 Pacific Jazz themes, Inter/Classic typography, Sidebar/Dock navigation, 4 cartography layers) Any signed-in user Travel Engine & Optimization Solver Constraints & Pacing (walking cap, tempo, meal windows, fatigue thresholds) and City Data (POIs, Valhalla OSM tiles, compiled GTFS feeds, disk vault) Admin only AI & Swarm Intelligence AI & LLM Engine (13 optional chat LLM providers, hardware RAM profile, Ollama unload) Admin only Sovereign Infrastructure & Admin Authorized Users, System Updates, Data Vault & Backups (snapshots + Immich/Synology photo sync), Notifications (Pushify, Pushover, Ntfy, Custom Webhooks), and API Keys & Secrets Admin only

docs.text:
