docs.title: Integrations, photo sync, and notification relays
docs.text: Connect self-hosted Immich and Synology Photos servers for automated trip album synchronization, configure outbound push relays across Pushify, Pushover, Ntfy, and Custom Webhooks, and manage external Travelpayouts and transit fare API keys in Settings (/config).

docs.title: Synchronizing trip photos with Immich and Synology
docs.text:
Paladio syncs trip galleries bidirectionally against self-hosted photo vaults from Settings (/config under Data Vault & Backups -> Photo Sync), storing configuration safely in PostgreSQL system_config.

ImmichSynology Photos / WebDAV
  1. Generate an Immich API key from your Immich Account Settings -> API Keys.
  2. In Paladio Settings -> Data Vault & Backups -> Photo Sync, enable Immich, enter your Immich server base URL (immich_url) and API key (immich_api_key), and specify the target album name (immich_album_name, default Paladio Vault).
  3. Click Test Connection (POST /api/system/photo-sync/test), then run Sync All Vault Photos (POST /api/system/photo-sync/sync-all) to upload existing expedition galleries.
  1. Enable WebDAV or DSM access for a dedicated service user on your Synology NAS.
  2. In Paladio Settings -> Data Vault & Backups -> Photo Sync, enable Synology, fill in synology_url, synology_username, synology_password, and synology_destination_path (default /photo/Paladio).
  3. Click Test Connection and save to sync uploaded trip photos automatically.

docs.title: Configuring outbound notification relays
docs.text:
Receive real-time alerts outside the web UI whenever the Deal Engine flags a P10 flight+hotel package, a trip changes, a booking pass finishes scanning, or photo sync completes.

  1. Open Settings (/config under Notifications -> Notification Types) and choose which event categories emit outbound relays (Deal Alerts, Trip Updates, Ticket Parsing, Photo Sync).
  2. Configure one or more delivery channels in the remaining sub-tabs:
  3. Pushify: Enter your Pushify endpoint/API token.
  4. Pushover & Ntfy: Configure a Pushover application + user token (api.pushover.net/1/messages.json), or point Ntfy to https://ntfy.sh or your self-hosted Ntfy instance and topic.
  5. Custom Webhooks: Supply any HTTPS webhook receiver URL for JSON event delivery.
  6. Click Test Delivery (POST /api/system/notifications/test) on each enabled channel to confirm payloads arrive cleanly.

docs.title: Managing API keys and external secrets
docs.text:
Open Settings (/config under API Keys & Secrets) to store optional external provider credentials dynamically in PostgreSQL system_config (key="secrets") without restarting containers.

  • Travelpayouts / Aviasales (aviasales): Enter your affiliate/data token to unlock cached route price sweeps in /monitoring; Paladio loads this token at startup and exposes a live test button (POST /api/system/secrets/test/aviasales) plus an environment-override indicator when TRAVELPAYOUTS_TOKEN or AVIASALES_TOKEN is already set in .env.
  • DeepL / LibreTranslate: Set DEEPL_API_KEY or LIBRETRANSLATE_URL in .env when you want on-demand translation (POST /api/pois/{poi_id}/translate) for foreign-language POI descriptions.
  • Tokyo ODPT (odpt): Supply ODPT_API_KEY / ODPT_CONSUMER_KEY in .env if you compile Tokyo GTFS schedules and want official dynamic rail fare lookups via the ODPT adapter.

docs.title: Configuring LLM providers and MCP clients
docs.text: Configure any of Paladio's 13 optional generative AI providers inside Settings (/config under AI & Swarm Intelligence) and connect external desktop or CLI agents such as Claude Desktop to Paladio's 82-tool Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

docs.title: Configuring optional chat LLM providers
docs.text:
Generative Large Language Models (LLMs) power only the interactive Plan -> Agent conversational assistant (TripAgentRunner), never deterministic trip generation or semantic embeddings.

  1. Open Settings (/config) as an administrator and click AI & LLM Engine.
  2. Choose one of the 13 supported providers: OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek, Mistral AI, OpenRouter, xAI (Grok), Perplexity, Together AI, Cerebras, Custom OpenAI Compatible / vLLM / LocalAI, or Ollama (Local).
  3. Enter your API key (or base URL for Custom OpenAI / Ollama) and select or type a model identifier.
  4. Click Test Connection (POST /api/system/llm/test) before saving so Paladio verifies authentication and model availability.

Local Ollama RAM guardrails and unloading

For local Ollama, HardwareService inspects host RAM, CPU cores, and GPU memory to compute safe num_ctx, num_thread, and keep_alive settings automatically. Use Unload Model (POST /api/system/llm/unload) in /config anytime to free VRAM/RAM for Valhalla or large PBF imports.

docs.title: Connecting external clients over Streamable HTTP (/mcp)
docs.text:
FastMCP mounts on the FastAPI gateway at POST/GET /mcp (mount_mcp_app), exposing all 82 tools, 6 resources, and 6 prompts to external MCP-capable applications authenticated with a Bearer JWT token.

  1. Sign into Paladio or obtain an access token via POST /api/auth/login.
  2. Point your MCP client to http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp with an Authorization: Bearer your_jwt_access_token_here header.
  3. Keep connections targeting localhost or 127.0.0.1 unless configuring an SSH tunnel or reverse proxy update, because verify_origin_and_host rejects untrusted Host and Origin headers to prevent DNS rebinding attacks.

docs.title: Connecting Claude Desktop via stdio (python -m app.mcp)
docs.text:
For local desktop clients like Claude Desktop that spawn MCP servers over stdio, invoke app.mcp directly inside the api container or your local virtual environment using PALADIO_API_TOKEN.

  1. Add a shared secret token (PALADIO_API_TOKEN) to the api service environment in .env and restart the container.
  2. Add the Paladio server entry to your claude_desktop_config.json:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "paladio": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": [
        "compose",
        "-f",
        "/path/to/paladio/docker-compose.yml",
        "exec",
        "-T",
        "-e",
        "PALADIO_API_TOKEN=your_paladio_api_token_here",
        "api",
        "python",
        "-m",
        "app.mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
  1. Restart Claude Desktop and verify the paladio tools (get_trip_overview, search_pois, optimize_day, what_if) and prompts (review_my_trip, rainy_day_plan) appear in the connector list.

Safe handling of Tier C tools in external MCP clients

When an external MCP client invokes a Tier C tool without confirmed=true (such as optimize_trip, swap_days, remove_day, fit_to_budget, or delete_ticket), the tool returns a pending ProposalData ID (paladio:proposal:{id}, valid for 600s) describing the proposed impact instead of executing immediately.

See MCP server reference for the complete catalog of 82 tools, 6 resources, and 6 prompts.

docs.title: Reverse proxy, security, and access control
docs.text: Expose Paladio safely behind Caddy, Nginx, or Traefik with WebSocket upgrade support for /api/ws/* and /mcp, enforce production cryptographic keys, manage trip Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and reset locked-out passwords from the server CLI.

docs.title: Production security checklist
docs.text:
Running Paladio on a LAN or public domain with ENVIRONMENT=production activates strict startup and encryption invariants across backend/app/core/.

  1. Generate dedicated secrets: Set high-entropy values for POSTGRES_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET_KEY (openssl rand -hex 32), and WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY (valid 32-byte URL-safe base64 Fernet key generated via python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"). In production, get_fernet() refuses to start if WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing.
  2. Restrict CORS origins: Set ALLOWED_ORIGINS to your exact HTTPS origin (https://paladio.example.com) so browser requests from unknown origins are rejected.
  3. Keep public registration closed: Leave ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION=false (the default) and create household or team accounts from Settings (/config under Authorized Users).
  4. Bind internal services locally: docker-compose.yml binds PostgreSQL (5432), Redis (6379), and Valhalla (8002) strictly to 127.0.0.1 so only frontend (3000) and api (8000) accept external proxy traffic.

Dockerfile production target healthcheck note

The production target in backend/Dockerfile defines HEALTHCHECK CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1 on python:3.12-slim without installing curl in that stage. When running the published GHCR paladio-api image in Compose or Kubernetes, override the healthcheck with Python (python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/health')") or HTTP liveness probes.

docs.title: Reverse proxy configurations (with WebSockets)
docs.text:
Route /api/* and /mcp to 127.0.0.1:8000 (backend FastAPI) and all remaining traffic to 127.0.0.1:3000 (Next.js frontend), preserving Upgrade and Connection headers for /api/ws/stream and /api/ws/trip-agent/{trip_id}.

CaddyNginxTraefik (Docker labels) 
paladio.example.com {
    handle /api/* {
        reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8000
    }
    handle /mcp* {
        reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8000
    }
    handle {
        reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
    }
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name paladio.example.com;

    location /api/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
    }

    location /mcp {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_buffering off;
    }

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}

# Add these labels to your api and frontend services when routing via Traefik:
# api:
#   - "traefik.http.routers.paladio-api.rule=Host(`paladio.example.com`) && (PathPrefix(`/api`) || PathPrefix(`/mcp`))"
#   - "traefik.http.services.paladio-api.loadbalancer.server.port=8000"
# frontend:
#   - "traefik.http.routers.paladio-ui.rule=Host(`paladio.example.com`)"
#   - "traefik.http.services.paladio-ui.loadbalancer.server.port=3000"

docs.title: Authentication, trip RBAC, and password resets
docs.text:
Paladio protects user credentials with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (100,000 iterations, 32-byte random salt, constant-time hmac.compare_digest), HS256 JWTs, and three-tier per-trip access control (core/access.py).

  • Trip access levels: OWNER (trip.user_id == user.id), EDITOR (any TripParticipantModel linked to that user account), and VIEWER (read-only access enforced by assert_trip_access). Legacy local trips with trip.user_id IS NULL grant local owner access automatically in single-user self-hosted deployments.
  • Sovereign CLI password reset: If an administrator loses their password, reset it directly on the host without external recovery emails:
docker compose exec api python scripts/reset_password.py admin new_strong_password_here

docs.title: Optional AI Travel Assistant (Plan -> Agent)
docs.text: Chat with the optional Paladio Travel Assistant inside Plan -> Agent to query nearby venues, diagnose schedule issues, dry-run changes, or propose multi-stop edits with explicit confirmation cards, countdown timers, and one-click revision undo.

docs.title: Deterministic planning versus optional chat LLMs
docs.text:
Paladio never hands arithmetic, distance matrices, or combinatorial ordering to a generative Large Language Model (LLM). Instead, TripAgentRunner (pydantic-ai) acts as a conversational orchestrator over the same deterministic FastMCP tools (paladio_core, Valhalla, GTFS, PostgreSQL) that power the rest of the workspace.

  • If you run Paladio solely for automated trip creation, booking scanning, route monitoring, and manual Speed Dial editing, you do not need to configure any LLM provider.
  • When you configure one or more LLM providers in Settings (/config under AI & LLM Engine), Plan -> Agent streams answers over WS /api/ws/trip-agent/{trip_id} and hot-switches models anytime from the header ModelSelectorPopover.

docs.title: Supported LLM providers and viewport context
docs.text:
The assistant header displays your active model pill and a removable ContextChip summarizing what you are currently viewing in /trips/[id].

  • 13 supported providers: OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek, Mistral AI, OpenRouter, xAI (Grok), Perplexity, Together AI, Cerebras, Custom OpenAI Compatible / vLLM / LocalAI, and local Ollama (guarded by HardwareService RAM checks).
  • UI viewport awareness: Each chat turn can pass your active tab, selected day, selected stop ID, destination, and current map bounding box (ui_context) so prompts like Find a quiet lunch near what I am looking at resolve against your exact screen state.
  • Dynamic toolset loading: Every turn starts with 21 core read/edit tools and dynamically loads specialized domain toolsets (expenses, tickets, transit, collab, collections, market, jobs, engine, itinerary_advanced) based on prompt keywords or the load_toolset tool.

docs.title: Confirmation safeguards, expiry timers, and instant Undo
docs.text:
Every mutation performed by the assistant creates an immutable snapshot in trip_revisions and logs SHA-256-hashed tool arguments in agent_actions, while high-impact ("Tier C") edits always pause for explicit approval before modifying your trip.

Safeguard layer Triggered when What you see in the UI Read-only & dry-run tools Queries (get_trip_issues, search_pois, what_if, compare_metrics) Executes immediately; displays live tool status pills and inline POI result cards Tier W routine writes Low-risk edits (adding an unlocked stop, setting stop notes, updating preferences) Executes immediately, writes a trip_revisions snapshot, and pops a 10s ChangeToast with an Undo button Tier C confirmation gate High-impact or destructive tools (remove_stop on locked/anchor stops, swap_days, remove_day, optimize_trip, rebalance_days, fit_to_budget, delete_ticket, delete_expense, remove_participant, change_hotel_anchor, update_trip_details for destination/dates, export_trip_package shareable) Pauses on a CONFIRMATION REQUIRED ProposalCard showing an itemized JSON diff preview, countdown timer (600s backend Redis TTL; 300s fallback timer if omitted), and Reject / Approve Change buttons

Follow these steps to work safely with the assistant:

  1. Open /trips/[id], select Plan -> Agent, and verify your preferred model pill (or click it to switch via ModelSelectorPopover).
  2. Ask a question or request a schedule change (for example, What issues does Day 2 have? or Rebalance stops so Day 3 has less walking).
  3. Review any CONFIRMATION REQUIRED ProposalCard diff carefully before clicking Approve Change or Reject.
  4. Click Undo on the post-mutation ChangeToast (or ask the agent to undo_last_change) if you want to revert immediately, or click Clear Chat History to reset the Redis conversation buffer (paladio:agent:session:{trip_id}:{user_id}).

docs.title: Bookings Wallet, scanning, and scannable passes
docs.text: Store boarding passes, hotel confirmations, door PINs, attraction tickets, and Apple Wallet .pkpass bundles inside the Wallet tab of /trips/[id], scan barcodes locally with zero cloud OCR calls, and display high-contrast passes at airport gates.

docs.title: Importing tickets into WalletDropzone
docs.text:
Paladio extracts reservation metadata deterministically on your server using zxing-cpp for 1D/2D barcodes and tesseract-ocr + poppler-utils for PDFs and screenshots, keeping personal travel documents private.

  1. Open the Wallet tab inside /trips/[id].
  2. Drag and drop PDF, PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, TXT, or Apple Wallet .pkpass files into WalletDropzone, or click + ADD PASS to enter details manually or paste raw email confirmation text.
  3. Review every extracted field (flight carrier, route, departure/arrival timestamps, PNR, seat, terminal/gate, venue, and decoded barcode payload) inside ScanReviewModal.
  4. Confirm the draft to save it to trip_tickets and attach original uploaded files to trip_ticket_attachments (persisted on disk under WALLET_STORAGE_DIR).

docs.title: Supported ticket categories and specialized cards
docs.text:
TripWalletView renders tailored cards per booking category, tracks the next scheduled travel event in WalletUpNext, and surfaces gate or transit advisories automatically.

Category filter Card component Key fields and behaviors Flights FlightBoardingPassCard Origin/destination IATA codes, flight number, terminal/gate, seat, PNR, and boarding barcode Stays & Keys HotelAccessCard Check-in/out times, room/unit, plus Fernet-encrypted door PINs and Wi-Fi passwords masked behind SecretField with one-click copy Attractions AttractionPassCard Timed-entry slot, venue address, reservation code, and entry QR/barcode Transit TransitTicketCard Rail/bus/ferry operator, route/zone, validity window, and scannable fare pass Other GenericTicketCard Insurance policies, rental cars, tours, or custom notes and attachments

docs.title: Displaying fullscreen scannable codes and syncing anchors
docs.text:
At airport security, boarding gates, or museum turnstiles, you can filter passes instantly and pop out high-contrast barcodes without zooming a PDF.

  • Filter and search: Click All, Flights, Stays & Keys, Attractions, Transit, or Other pills, or type a confirmation code, venue, or flight number into the search bar.
  • Fullscreen scannable barcode: Click any ticket card to open TicketDetailModal, where CodeRenderer renders crisp QR, Aztec, PDF417, Code128, or DataMatrix codes alongside original PDF/image attachments.
  • Sync to itinerary: Click SYNC ITINERARY (or RE-SYNC ITINERARY) to align your trip's flight windows, hotel check-in/out depot times, and timed attraction anchors with your verified wallet passes.

Protect your secrets when sharing .trip packages

Ticket access codes (access_code, Wi-Fi keys, door PINs) are encrypted at rest with Fernet (WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY) and masked in MCP tool outputs. When exporting a .trip archive from Share Expedition, choose Shareable (community_shareable) to strip all PNR codes, raw barcodes, holder names, and ticket attachments, or Full Vault (full_vault) only for personal encrypted backups.

docs.title: Control Center and Taste Star
docs.text: Navigate Paladio's application shell, interpret your 8-axis Taste Star radar, schedule expeditions on the operations Calendar with public holidays and Paid Time Off (PTO) markers, and manage saved Point of Interest (POI) collections from /dashboard.

docs.title: Application navigation shell and appearance
docs.text:
Paladio adapts its global navigation, theme palette, typography, and language direction dynamically per account so the workspace matches your preferred reading density and screen size.

  • Collapsible Sidebar or Floating Dock: Switch between the left AppSidebar (toggle with Ctrl+B or Cmd+B) and the bottom hover-reveal FloatingDock inside Settings (/config). Both expose Control Center (/dashboard), New Trip (/engine), Route Monitoring (/monitoring), and Trip Archive (/vault), while the user menu links to Settings (/config), Help Center (/help), and Sign Out.
  • Pacific Jazz themes and typography: Choose Pacific Jazz Light, Pacific Jazz Dark, or Silent Waters, and pair them with Inter (universal multi-script stack) or Classic (Jost display + Inter body + JetBrains Mono).
  • 10 shipped locales with RTL support: Switch between Arabic (ar, flips <html dir="rtl"> automatically), Chinese Simplified (zh-CN), English (en), French (fr), German (de), Italian (it), Japanese (ja), Korean (ko), Portuguese (pt), and Spanish (es).
  • Global notifications: Click the header bell icon to open the slide-out notification center (persisted up to 100 items per user in localStorage) for deal alerts, GTFS transit build completions, POI hydration jobs, and ticket scans.

docs.title: Control Center widgets
docs.text:
Every widget on /dashboard pulls live state from PostgreSQL, pgvector semantic matching, and Celery Beat market telemetry.

Widget Source data Primary action Active Trip Ticket Next upcoming or active trip in PostgreSQL Click the boarding-ticket hero card to launch /trips/[id] with countdown, waypoint count, participant roster, and local timezone Taste Star UserTasteProfileModel 8-axis preference vector View scores across 8 travel categories alongside Travel Pace and Budget Strategy badges Best Offer Card Lowest verified 10th-percentile (P10) deal in /monitoring Inspect destination savings and jump straight to Route Monitoring or pre-fill New Trip (/engine) Recommended POIs 768-dimensional ONNX vector cosine match in pgvector Browse personalized attractions with verified Wikimedia photos, % Taste Match, and Add to Trip Upcoming Trips Active and draft expeditions Open a workspace or delete an unused draft Saved Collections Global TripCollectionModel lists (trip_id IS NULL) Organize reusable place wishlists or import stops into a trip

docs.title: Seed and tune your 8-axis Taste Star
docs.text:
When an account starts with a neutral preference vector (0.5 across all axes), Control Center displays a calibration banner linking to /taste-calibration.

  1. Open /taste-calibration and answer up to 8 scenario prompts (first_morning, afternoon_pace, urban_form, dining_style, after_sunset, markets_craft, budget_strategy, and crowd_discovery), skipping any dimension you want to keep neutral.
  2. Inspect your updated radar across art_culture, history_heritage, nature_outdoors, architecture, food_culinary, nightlife, shopping, and scenic_views.
  3. As you bookmark POIs into collections, complete trips, or set likes and vetoes via the optional assistant, Paladio updates your UserTasteProfileModel and retrains ranker weights nightly via Celery Beat.
  4. Export, reset to neutral, or delete your stored taste history anytime from Settings (/config) or the /api/users/me/taste endpoints.

Deterministic guardrails never sacrifice logistics for taste

High % Taste Match boosts a venue's priority during candidate selection, yet the C++20 solver enforces opening hours, meal spacing, walking fatigue limits, and district clustering so schedules stay realistic.

docs.title: Operations Calendar, public holidays, and PTO mode
docs.text:
The interactive Calendar on /dashboard overlays active trips, archived trips, monitored P10 flight deals, statutory public holidays for your configured country, and personal PTO days across both an annual dispatch grid and a focused monthly view.

  1. Set your statutory holiday country under Settings (/config in Personal Account).
  2. Enable Holiday Mode on the Calendar to click dates and toggle personal PTO days, or clear an entire year's PTO selections in one click.
  3. Click any open calendar date to open /engine?start_date=YYYY-MM-DD, click any highlighted deal bar to jump directly to /monitoring?route=<route_id>, or export all trips and monitored deal windows into a single .ics calendar file.

docs.title: Costs, live currency conversion, and group splitting
docs.text: Compare actual expenses against your target budget in the Costs tab of /trips/[id], convert currencies with live European Central Bank (ECB) rates, assign planned route estimates into real ledger entries, scan receipts, and settle group debts with minimal transfers.

docs.title: Reading cost summary cards and category breakdowns
docs.text:
TripCostsView separates projected route admissions from recorded expenses so you always see both committed spending and remaining headroom.

Dashboard card What it tracks Pending costs / All costs paid Itinerary stops with estimated entry prices that have not yet been assigned as paid expenses You owe / You're owed / All settled up Your net group balance across all Crew Roster splits in the trip ledger Total trip spend Recorded expenses vs target budget, paired with CategoryBreakdownWidget across flights, accommodation, transport, food, activities, sightseeing, and other

Use the Live Currency Exchange (LIVE ECB) bar and 3D CurrencyWheelPicker to preview every figure across currencies in real time without altering stored receipt amounts.

docs.title: Assigning route estimates and scanning receipts
docs.text:
You do not need to re-type admission costs or transit estimates already present in your itinerary.

  1. Scroll to any unassigned Route Estimate card in Costs and click Assign to convert that planned stop estimate into a recorded expense item (choose payer and participants).
  2. Click Add expense (ExpenseModal) to log a new transaction manually, or upload a receipt image/PDF (POST /api/trips/{trip_id}/expenses/scan-receipt) to pre-fill merchant, total amount, currency, and date via Tesseract OCR.
  3. Filter recorded entries by category, payer, or search query via CostsFilterToolbar, or click Export CSV to download the full ledger for external accounting.

docs.title: Splitting expenses and settling group balances
docs.text:
Paladio computes exact per-person shares across your trip's Crew Roster (trip_participants) and simplifies multi-party debts into the fewest possible bank transfers.

  1. Open Add expense (or edit an existing entry), pick who paid, and choose Equal or Custom split amounts across selected Crew Roster members.
  2. Inspect BalancesWidget to verify each traveler's net position (GET /api/trips/{trip_id}/settlement).
  3. Click Settle up to open SettlementModal, which lists the minimal sequence of peer-to-peer transfers required to bring every participant's balance to zero.

docs.title: Public transit and Valhalla routing
docs.text: Inspect step-by-step metro, rail, tram, and bus routes, browse local transit lines, check real-time-style station departures, and compute street-level walking legs inside Plan -> Transit powered by self-hosted Valhalla, Transitous, and locally compiled GTFS schedules.

docs.title: How Paladio combines Valhalla, GTFS, and Transitous
docs.text:
Unlike cloud trip planners that hit external commercial API quotas, Paladio computes street-level walking and driving matrices locally while compiling official open transit schedules into PostgreSQL.

Layer Engine / Source What it powers Walking and road routing Self-hosted valhalla container + OSM PBF extracts Accurate footpath distances, door-to-door walking leg durations, and travel matrices for the C++20 solver Local transit schedules Compiled GTFS feeds derived into 14 PostgreSQL tables Sub-second offline-capable queries for Directions, Lines, Nearby stations, stop timetables, and map overlays Live fallback routing Transitous (api.transitous.org) with Redis cache Supplements transit leg routing when a destination lacks a compiled local GTFS feed Transit fare estimation 5-tier FareResolver (GTFS fares + ODPT Tokyo + TfL London + cited official quotes) Accurate per-leg transit cost estimation and daily pass vs single-ticket advice

docs.title: Three transit modes inside Plan -> Transit
docs.text:
Open the Transit tab in your workspace sidebar to switch between point-to-point routing, full network line exploration, and station departure boards.

Tab mode Inputs and filters Output Directions Any two itinerary stops or custom coordinates, day selector, Depart at or Arrive by time Multimodal itinerary combining exact walking transfers, line headsigns, stop counts, and leg durations Lines Independent Metro, Rail, Tram, and Bus mode chips Agency-grouped network routes; clicking a line draws its full alignment and ordered station sequence on the map Nearby Active map viewport or Speed Dial Area Filter Closest transit stations with walking distance and upcoming scheduled departures

docs.title: Filter by transit mode and Speed Dial waypoint area
docs.text:
Use mode chips and spatial area filtering together to isolate transit options around a hotel or neighborhood before locking stops.

  1. Click any combination of Metro, Rail, Tram, and Bus chips at the top of the Transit tab (all four toggle independently).
  2. Expand the bottom-left Speed Dial (+) on the map and click DROP WAYPOINT to place a spatial radius circle over a district you want to explore.
  3. Activate Area Filter in Transit so Nearby stations and lines snap strictly to that circle, then click any station pin or card to inspect serving lines and upcoming departures.

docs.title: Checking and compiling GTFS city coverage
docs.text:
At the top of Plan -> Transit, Paladio shows the GTFS build status for your destination city (READY, BUILDING, QUEUED, or UNAVAILABLE).

  • Automatic sync for planned trips: Administrators can compile GTFS feeds for all upcoming cities at once from Settings (/config under City Data) using Sync Planned Trips GTFS.
  • Upgrading existing itineraries: After a city's GTFS feed finishes compiling in the transit_build queue, trigger POST /api/trips/{trip_id}/upgrade-transit (or use the upgrade_trip_transit agent tool) to replace estimated transit legs with real compiled schedule connections.
  • Manual city compilation: See Managing city POIs, Valhalla maps, and GTFS for queue locks, storage cleanup, and cities without public open GTFS feeds.

docs.title: Route monitoring and deal packages
docs.text:
Monitor round-trip flight and lodging corridors continuously at /monitoring, evaluate fare drops against 10th-percentile (P10) quantile baselines, inspect multi-month bidirectional calendars, and convert verified packages directly into trips in /engine.

Experimental data scraping

The underlying flight and lodging data scraping in Route Monitoring is currently experimental. External provider scrapers and rate feeds may be unstable or incomplete depending on upstream changes and configured API keys.

docs.title: Fleet KPI cards and monitored routes table
docs.text:
Celery Beat triggers the daily market pipeline (daily_market_pipeline_task) at 03:00 UTC (plus on-demand corridor sweeps and backfills), storing historical price ticks inside a TimescaleDB hypertable (market_price_ticks).

Telemetry surface What it reports Monitored Routes Count of active and paused origin-to-destination corridors tracked for your account Open Deal Alerts Active corridors whose verified fare sits below the 10th-percentile (P10) baseline threshold Ticks Scanned Today Total flight and lodging price observations collected in the current sweep window Average Savings Mean percentage discount across open deals compared against each corridor's 30-day median (P50)

Filter the route table using ALL, DEAL, ACTIVE, or PAUSED pills, or search by origin/destination IATA code. Each route renders a VerdictBadge (GREAT, GOOD, TYPICAL, HIGH, PEAK) alongside its live percentile (P<N>) and baseline maturity (building, provisional, or established).

docs.title: Creating a monitored corridor
docs.text:
Define airport pairs, trip duration constraints, and per-passenger ceiling budgets so the Deal Engine ignores mismatched red-eyes or budget overruns.

  1. Open /monitoring and click + Monitor Route.
  2. Choose Origin and Destination airports using live airport resolution.
  3. Configure either a flexible date horizon or bounded departure dates, set minimum and maximum stay nights (1 to 30), traveler count, and your per-passenger budget ceiling with the currency picker.
  4. Click Save (POST /api/market/routes) to trigger initial corpus backfill (backfill_route_corpus_task) and lodging prewarming (prewarm_route_lodging_task).

Configuring Aviasales / Travelpayouts keys

Flight cache sweeps and live verifiers use your Travelpayouts/Aviasales token configured in Settings (/config under API Keys & Secrets) alongside Ryanair public fares and multi-provider hotel scrapers (Booking, Google Travel, Agoda, Trip.com).

docs.title: Acting on verified deal packages
docs.text:
When outbound and return flight fares align with a quality-gated hotel stay and the landed package drops below the P10 target, /monitoring highlights a VERIFIED DEAL PACKAGE FOUND banner (and surfaces the best offer on Control Center).

  • Make it a Trip: Pre-fills /engine via query parameters with exact outbound/inbound flight dates, airport times, verified lodging anchor, and package budget so you can generate a matching daily itinerary in one pass.
  • Discard Offer: Dismisses that candidate alert (POST /api/market/deals/{deal_id}/discard) and records implicit negative deal feedback (POST /api/market/deals/{deal_id}/feedback) to refine future package verdicts.

docs.title: Full-screen route inspection and bidirectional calendars
docs.text:
Click Inspect on any corridor to launch RouteFullScreenView, pairing historical curve telemetry with date-by-date round-trip exploration.

  1. Toggle 24h, 7d, 30d, or 90d on PriceTrendGraph to compare recent sweeps against historical quantile bands (q02 through q90).
  2. Switch MonitoringCalendar between Outbound, Inbound, and Roundtrip modes across multiple months to spot cheap departure/return pairs visually.
  3. Click any calendar date to fetch live lodging rate observations (GET /api/market/routes/{route_id}/lodging) and compare combined flight + stay totals before booking.
  4. Pause, resume, manually scan (POST /api/market/routes/{route_id}/scan), backfill (POST /api/market/routes/{route_id}/backfill), or delete the route from the inspection header.

docs.title: Creating trips and intake workflows
docs.text: Launch a Personalized Trip powered by the deterministic 9-node LangGraph swarm and C++20 optimizer, start from a Blank Trip canvas, or bootstrap an itinerary from flight confirmations, .pkpass tickets, and .trip archives at /engine.

docs.title: Personalized Trip versus Blank Trip
docs.text:
/engine offers two creation modes, persisting your unsaved form state automatically in localStorage (useTripDraftStore) so navigating away never loses your route draft.

  • Personalized Trip: Executes the deterministic swarm over WS /api/ws/stream, streaming live ThinkingScreen stages (PARSING_TICKETS, EXTRACTING_CONSTRAINTS, VERIFYING_CONSTRAINTS, EVALUATING_GUARDRAILS, ANALYZING_PROMPT, SCRAPING_DYNAMIC_DATA, EVALUATING_ROUTES) before opening /trips/[id].
  • Blank Trip: Creates an empty expedition shell immediately for manual curation in the Trip Workspace without waiting for route optimization.

docs.title: Structured trip intake fields
docs.text:
Every intake card on /engine maps directly to constraints consumed by the 8-stage Itinerary v2 pipeline and C++20 TCOPTW solver.

Intake control What it configures How the engine uses it Cover Banner Custom expedition header image or reset Stored as the trip cover across Control Center, Workspace, and Archive recaps Flight Route Bar ORIG / DEST airport IATA codes plus arrival and departure hours Constrains Day 1 start time after landing and final-day end time before airport departure Hotel Stay Anchor Hotel search or map pin selection with check-in and check-out times Sets the daily start and return depot coordinate (NodeType.HOTEL) for optimize_itinerary Budget & Currency Wheel Target budget amount and 3D currency picker Allocates pro-rata daily spending caps with live FX conversion against POI admission prices Crew Roster Linked Paladio user accounts and guest companions Merges participant taste profiles during selection and initializes group expense splitting Travel Window Calendar date range picker Sets trip duration (<= 30 days guardrail) and seasonal weather / holiday context Intent Prompt Natural-language preferences and preset chips Processed deterministically by PromptIntentExtractor using 768-D ONNX anchor projection and rapidfuzz POI matching

Where Exploration Pace lives

You adjust a specific trip's daily tempo (Relaxed, Balanced, or Packed / High Tempo) inside that trip's Configuration tab after creation. Global default walking caps, meal deadlines, and fatigue multipliers live in Settings (/config under Solver Constraints & Pacing).

docs.title: Uploading bookings, .pkpass, and .trip packages
docs.text:
Instead of typing flights and stays manually, click the upload icon (+) on /engine to import travel documents or previously exported expeditions.

  1. Drop PDF, PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, TXT, or JSON booking files, Apple Wallet .pkpass bundles, or .trip archives into the modal, or paste raw confirmation email text directly.
  2. Wait for the deterministic local scanner (zxing-cpp for IATA BCBP barcodes, tesseract-ocr + poppler-utils for PDFs and images, and regex extractors for text) to populate origin, destination, dates, and hotel anchors.
  3. For .trip packages (application/vnd.paladio.trip+zip), Paladio restores the itinerary, collections, photos, and (for full_vault exports) wallet passes and expenses directly into a new trip workspace.

docs.title: Safety and human-in-the-loop checkpoints
docs.text:
During Personalized Trip generation, the LangGraph swarm can pause or halt via structured interactive modals when validation checks detect conflicts.

  • Verification Required (verify_constraints interrupt): Presents extracted dates, airports, budget, and hotel anchor for confirmation or last-second edits before scraping and C++ solving start.
  • Trip Overlap Warning (guardrails interrupt): Alerts you when your requested dates collide with an existing trip stored in PostgreSQL so you can cancel or proceed intentionally.
  • Guardrail Abort: Rejects invalid spans immediately (dates in the past, return date earlier than start date, identical origin and destination, or trips exceeding 30 days).

docs.title: Launching trips from Calendar and Route Monitoring
docs.text:
You can pre-fill /engine with one click from other views using URL query parameters handled by dealToTrip.ts:

  • From Control Center Calendar: Clicking a calendar date opens /engine?start_date=YYYY-MM-DD.
  • From Route Monitoring: Clicking Make it a Trip on a VERIFIED DEAL PACKAGE FOUND banner or Best Offer Card preloads the deal's origin, destination, outbound/inbound flight dates, hotel anchor, and package budget into /engine.

docs.title: Trip Workspace, map controls, and editing
docs.text: Manage your active itinerary inside /trips/[id] using the Leaflet + MapLibre GL 2D map, 6-tab Plan sidebar, bottom-left Speed Dial (EDIT ROUTE, DROP WAYPOINT, VIEW), custom POI creator, external navigation launchers, and IndexedDB offline pinning.

docs.title: Workspace header and top-level tabs
docs.text:
Every trip workspace opens to a full-screen layout with a compact top bar linking the five operational views of your expedition.

Header control Purpose Plan Pairs the 6-tab left planning sidebar (Route, Search, Transit, Weather, Collections, Agent) with the interactive route map Wallet Stores boarding passes, hotel keys, attraction tickets, .pkpass bundles, and fullscreen scannable barcodes Costs Compares recorded expenses against your target budget, converts live ECB rates, and calculates group debt settlements Photos Displays local uploads and albums synchronized from Immich or Synology Photos Configuration Edits flight windows, hotel anchor, Exploration Pace, budget, Crew Roster, trip status, and activity revision history Offline Pin button Downloads trip JSON, Wallet passes, ticket attachments, and expenses into browser IndexedDB for offline access Share Expedition Opens exports for .trip packages, Printable PDF Dossier, .ics, .gpx, and .json

Completed trips redirect to /vault/[id]

Once you mark an expedition Completed (Archived in Vault) inside Configuration, navigating to /trips/[id] automatically redirects to its read-only recap at /vault/[id]. Append ?workspace=1 to reopen the full live editor anytime.

docs.title: Navigating the six sidebar tabs inside Plan
docs.text:
All daily scheduling, discovery, weather checks, and agent edits share the left panel inside Plan, syncing selection state with the map markers on the right.

  1. Route: Displays ALL DAYS, day tabs (DAY 1, DAY 2, …), + Day to extend your trip, hotel anchors, numbered stop cards, and clickable transit leg connectors showing walk or GTFS transit steps.
  2. Search: Queries destination POIs with category chips, rating/duration/price filters, sort controls, a Custom filter toggle, bookmark buttons, and Add POI to drop a custom pin anywhere on the map.
  3. Transit: Provides Directions, Lines, and Nearby views powered by Valhalla and compiled GTFS feeds. See Public transit and Valhalla routing.
  4. Weather: Fetches Open-Meteo daily forecasts, Air Quality Index (AQI) alerts, and travel advisories, or seasonal historical climate averages when your departure date lies beyond forecast range.
  5. Collections: Lets you browse saved or trip-scoped bookmark collections, track visit_status, import GPX/KML/KMZ or Google Maps lists, and insert saved places directly into any trip day.
  6. Agent: Opens the optional interactive AI Travel Assistant (TripAgentRunner) with viewport context injection and human-in-the-loop proposal cards.

docs.title: Editing routes with the bottom-left Speed Dial
docs.text:
Click the circular + Speed Dial button at the bottom-left corner of the map to unlock direct timeline editing, spatial filtering, and card density toggles.

Speed Dial toggle States Behavior Edit mode EDIT ROUTE / EDITING ACTIVE Reveals drag handles, lock buttons, delete buttons, and the Solve button on every day card Spatial radius DROP WAYPOINT / CLEAR AREA Places a draggable circle on the map with adjustable radius; filters both the Search and Transit tabs to that zone Card detail VIEW: SIMPLE / VIEW: DETAILED Switches between compact stop titles and expanded schedules with full transit connectors

Follow these steps to reshape a day without losing booked time slots:

  1. Expand the bottom-left Speed Dial (+) and activate EDIT ROUTE.
  2. Click the lock icon on fixed-time stops (such as timed museum tickets or restaurant bookings) so the optimizer treats them as immutable anchors.
  3. Drag stops to reorder them manually or remove unwanted stops.
  4. Click Solve to invoke the C++20 solve_tsptw (with solve_tsp_tour fallback) re-optimizer, which recalculates optimal stop ordering and walking or GTFS transit legs while honoring your locked stops.

docs.title: Inspecting POIs and launching external navigation
docs.text:
Clicking any card or map pin opens PoiDetailView with Wikimedia photos, opening hours, admission pricing provenance, description translation (via DeepL or LibreTranslate when configured), and direct navigation handoffs.

  • External navigation apps: Launch any stop's exact coordinates in Google Maps, Apple Maps, CoMaps / Organic Maps, OsmAnd, Waze, or Citymapper, or download a single-POI .gpx waypoint file.
  • Creating custom stops: Open Plan -> Search, click Add POI, pick exact coordinates on the location picker map, set duration and category, and save the custom pin exclusively to that trip without altering the shared global POI catalog.

docs.title: Offline PWA pinning and revision recovery
docs.text:
Paladio registers a Service Worker (sw.js) for static shell and map tile caching (OpenFreeMap, OpenStreetMap, Carto) and pairs it with IndexedDB (offlineStore.ts) for field reliability when cellular data drops.

  • Pin a trip offline: Click the offline pin icon in the workspace header before boarding; Paladio caches the full itinerary JSON, Wallet tickets, attached ticket files, and recorded expenses locally.
  • Revert or restore revisions: Every manual edit, drag reorder, re-optimization, and agent mutation creates an immutable snapshot in trip_revisions. Trigger Revert or Restore via the API or agent Undo to roll back safely.

docs.title: Trip Archive, Vault recaps, photos, and sharing
docs.text: Explore all completed expeditions on the interactive world map at /vault, review read-only recaps at /vault/[id], manage trip galleries with Immich or Synology Photo sync, and export trips in .trip, PDF, .ics, .gpx, or .json formats.

docs.title: World VaultMap and lifetime travel telemetry
docs.text:
When you mark a trip Completed (Archived in Vault) inside Configuration, it moves onto the global /vault map alongside cumulative travel statistics.

Vault telemetry metric Calculation All missions & Days logged Total archived expeditions and cumulative travel days across all completed trips Countries visited & Most engaged Highlighted world GeoJSON country polygons plus top visited destinations ranked by trip count and days Earth distance gauge Cumulative flight and route distance compared against Earth's equatorial circumference (40,075 km) Monthly breakdown Chronological timeline table grouping completed trips by month and destination

Click any destination in the collapsible General statistics drawer to fly the VaultMap camera directly to that country, or click a trip pin to open its recap at /vault/[id].

docs.title: Completed trip recaps (/vault/[id])
docs.text:
/vault/[id] renders PastTripRecap as a read-only chronicle with flight strips, route maps, and four focused tabs (About, Itinerary, Costs, Photos).

  1. Open About to read or edit your retrospective expedition narrative and private field notes.
  2. Browse Itinerary, Costs, and Photos for an archive view without accidental route edits.
  3. Append ?workspace=1 (or ?force=1) to /trips/[id] whenever you want to reopen the full editing workspace on a completed trip.

docs.title: Managing trip photos and NAS / Immich sync
docs.text:
The Photos tab inside both active workspaces (/trips/[id]) and Vault recaps (/vault/[id]) lets you upload local high-resolution images and synchronize albums from self-hosted photo servers.

  • Local uploads: Drag and drop images via PhotoUploadModal (POST /api/trips/{trip_id}/photos); Paladio serves them directly from disk (PHOTO_STORAGE_DIR).
  • Immich and Synology Photos sync: Configure server credentials in Settings (/config under Data Vault & Backups -> Photo Sync) so Paladio automatically matches trip dates to remote albums and pulls vault memories.

docs.title: Exporting and sharing via Share Expedition
docs.text:
Click Share Expedition from any trip header (/trips/[id] or /vault/[id]) to copy the workspace link or export portable files in five formats.

Export format What it includes Filtering and privacy options Paladio Package (.trip) Self-contained ZIP archive (application/vnd.paladio.trip+zip) with SHA-256 manifest, itinerary, collections, and photos Choose Full Vault (keeps private Wallet passes, receipts, and expenses) or Shareable (community_shareable, strips PNR/barcodes/attachments/expenses and anonymizes travelers) Printable Document (.pdf) Clean TripPrintDossier layout printed via browser print-to-PDF Formats daily schedules, addresses, and leg timings for offline paper backup Calendar Sync (.ics) RFC 5545 calendar events for timed stops and bookings Filter by All Days or select specific trip days GPX Track (.gpx) Waypoints and route tracks for Garmin, OsmAnd, CoMaps, and GPS apps Filter by All Days or select specific trip days Raw Itinerary (.json) Complete structured itinerary payload Filter by All Days or select specific trip days

See .trip file format specification for exact archive layout and sanitization details.
